operations.description:
Update the carrier name and tracking number for an existing shipment.

A seller can correct or update the tracking information — carrier name and tracking number — of a shipment they created, as long as delivery has not yet been confirmed. This allows sellers to fix data entry errors or update tracking numbers when the carrier provides a revised tracking number after the initial shipment creation.

Tracking information updates are only permitted before delivery confirmation. Once a customer confirms delivery — or the system automatically confirms delivery 14 days after the shipment was created — the tracking information becomes immutable. This ensures the historical accuracy of delivery records and prevents tampering with completed shipments.
operations.name: update
operations.specification:
Update the carrier_name and/or tracking_number on an existing shipment owned by the authenticated seller.

Authorization: The authenticated seller must be the creator of the shipment (shopping_mall_seller_id matches the authenticated seller's ID).

Preconditions:
- The shipment must exist and not be soft-deleted (deleted_at IS NULL). If not found, return 404.
- delivered_at must be null — shipments with confirmed delivery have immutable tracking information. If delivered_at IS NOT NULL, return 409 Conflict.

Implementation:
1. Query shopping_mall_shipments by id WHERE deleted_at IS NULL. If no record found, return 404.
2. Verify shopping_mall_seller_id matches the authenticated seller. If not, return 403 Forbidden.
3. Verify delivered_at IS NULL. If not, return 409 Conflict with message indicating tracking information is immutable after delivery confirmation.
4. Update carrier_name and/or tracking_number with the provided values. Both fields can be updated independently — at least one must be provided.
5. Set updated_at to the current timestamp.
6. Return the full updated shipment record.

Error codes:
- 404: Shipment not found (invalid id or soft-deleted record).
- 403: Authenticated seller does not own this shipment.
- 409: Delivery already confirmed — tracking information cannot be modified after delivery.

operations.description:
Request cancellation for a single order item.

Submits a cancellation request for an individual order item that is in "paid" status. Cancellation is processed per order item — other items in the same order continue through their normal lifecycle unaffected by this request.

The customer must provide a reason explaining why cancellation is requested. The request enters "pending" status and awaits review by the seller who owns the product. The seller may approve or reject the request. If approved, a refund is processed and the variant's stock quantity is restored via a positive inventory record.

Cancellation requests are only accepted while the order item remains in "paid" status. Once an item has been shipped (status "shipped") or reached any later state — "delivered", "cancelled", or "refunded" — cancellation is no longer available through this endpoint. After a rejection, customers may submit a new cancellation request for the same item.
operations.name: create
operations.specification:
Create a cancellation request for the specified order item.

1. Retrieve the order item from shopping_mall_order_items by itemId. If not found, respond 404.
2. Verify the order item status is exactly "paid". If the status is "shipped", "delivered", "cancelled", or "refunded", respond 422 with a message indicating cancellation is only available for items in "paid" status.
3. Verify the requesting customer owns the order containing this order item. Trace from shopping_mall_order_items → shopping_mall_orders → customer_id and compare against the authenticated customer's ID. If they do not match, respond 403.
4. Validate that the reason field in the request body is present, non-empty, and not only whitespace. If missing or blank, respond 422.
5. Insert a new row into shopping_mall_cancellation_requests:
   - id: newly generated UUID
   - shopping_mall_order_item_id: itemId from path
   - reason: customer-provided reason text
   - status: "pending"
   - created_at: current timestamp
   - updated_at: current timestamp
   - deleted_at: null
6. Return the newly created cancellation request record with all fields populated.

Error conditions:
- 404: order item not found
- 403: authenticated customer does not own the order
- 422: order item status is not "paid"
- 422: reason is missing, empty, or whitespace-only

The results returned depend on the actor making the request. Customers see only cancellation requests for items in their own orders, providing visibility into the status of their cancellation submissions. Sellers see cancellation requests for items from their products, enabling them to review and respond to pending requests for the items they sell. Administrators have platform-wide visibility and can see all cancellation requests across all sellers and customers.

Filters allow narrowing results by status (e.g., viewing only pending requests that require action), by specific order item, or by creation date range. The default sort order places the newest requests first, ensuring that the most recent submissions appear at the top. Soft-deleted cancellation request records are excluded from results by default, though the underlying records remain preserved for audit purposes.

The summary view includes the essential information needed for list display: the request identifier, associated order item reference, customer-provided reason, current status, and creation timestamp.

operations.description:
Seller responds to a pending cancellation request by approving or rejecting it.

A seller reviews a cancellation request submitted by a customer for one of their order items and makes a decision. The seller may approve the cancellation, which cancels the order item, processes a refund, and restores the variant's stock quantity via a positive inventory record. Alternatively, the seller may reject the cancellation, leaving the order item in its current "paid" status and allowing the customer to submit a new cancellation request for the same item later.

On response, the system creates an immutable snapshot preserving the cancellation request state at the moment of the seller's decision. This snapshot captures the reason text and the new status, serving as a permanent audit record for dispute resolution and accountability.

Only the seller who owns the product associated with the order item may respond to the cancellation request. The request must be in "pending" status — already-resolved requests (approved or rejected) cannot be responded to again.
operations.name: update
operations.specification:
Implement seller response to a cancellation request.

1. AUTHORIZATION: Verify the authenticated actor is a seller. Trace the ownership chain: cancellation request → order item → product variant → product → seller. Only the seller who owns the product may respond. Reject with 403 if the seller does not own the product. Suspended sellers may still process existing orders and respond to cancellation requests.

2. VALIDATION: Load the cancellation request by requestId. If not found, return 404. Verify the current status is "pending" — reject with 409 (Conflict) if already "approved" or "rejected" to prevent double-response. The request must not be soft-deleted (deleted_at IS NULL).

3. REQUEST BODY: Accept the seller's decision as the new status. Valid values are "approved" or "rejected". Reject any other value with 422.

4. STATUS TRANSITION: Update the cancellation request status to the seller's decision. Set updated_at to the current timestamp.

5. SNAPSHOT CREATION: Create a shopping_mall_cancellation_request_snapshot recording: the cancellation request ID (shopping_mall_cancellation_request_id), the reason text from the original request (preserved as-is), the new status ("approved" or "rejected"), and created_at as the current timestamp. Snapshots are permanently immutable — never update or delete them under any circumstance.

6. ON APPROVAL — INVENTORY RESTORATION: When the status transitions to "approved", create a positive inventory record for the product variant associated with the order item. The quantity change equals the order item's purchased quantity. The reason text should describe the cancellation approval context. The order item status transitions to "cancelled". All operations (status update, snapshot creation, inventory record creation, order item status change) must succeed or fail atomically — if any step fails, roll back the entire operation.

7. ON REJECTION: The order item remains in "paid" status. No inventory changes occur. The customer may submit a new cancellation request for the same order item later, provided the order item remains in "paid" status.

8. RESPONSE: Return the updated cancellation request entity with its new status, updated_at timestamp, and full details.

operations.description:
Submit a refund request for a delivered order item.

A refund request allows a customer to request a return and refund for an order item that has been delivered. The request is submitted per individual order item — different items within the same order require separate refund requests and are processed independently.

**Eligibility**: The targeted order item must be in `delivered` status and the request must be submitted within 7 calendar days from the date that item was marked as delivered. Orders still in `paid`, `shipped`, `cancelled`, or `refunded` status are not eligible.

**Request Content**: The customer must provide a reason explaining why the refund is sought. This reason is preserved immutably and is visible to the seller when reviewing the request. The reason cannot be empty or whitespace-only.

**Workflow**: Upon successful creation, the refund request enters the `pending` state. The seller of the item is notified and can respond by approving or rejecting the request. If approved, the payment is returned for that item, stock is restored via a positive inventory record, and the order item status changes to `refunded`. If rejected, the order item remains in `delivered` status with no changes. A snapshot of the request state is automatically created when the seller responds.

**Duplicate Prevention**: Only one refund request can be active per order item at a time. If a pending or approved refund request already exists for the same order item, the submission is rejected.
operations.name: create
operations.specification:
Implement customer-initiated refund request creation for a single order item.

**Authorization**: The authenticated customer must be the owner of the order containing the target order item. Verify via the FK chain: order_item → order → shopping_mall_customer_id matches the authenticated customer ID. Reject with 403 if the customer does not own the order.

**Item Status Validation**: Query the order item by `id` matching the `{itemId}` path parameter. Verify the order item's `status` is `delivered`. If the status is `paid`, `shipped`, or `cancelled`, respond with 422 and an appropriate message indicating the item is not eligible for refund. If the status is already `refunded`, respond with 409 (conflict). If the order item does not exist, respond with 404.

**Time Window Validation**: Calculate the 7-calendar-day refund window from the order item's most recent `updated_at` timestamp (which reflects when the status was last changed to `delivered`). Compare the current timestamp against this window. If more than 7 calendar days have elapsed, respond with 422 and a message indicating the refund window has expired.

**Duplicate Check**: Query `shopping_mall_refund_requests` for existing records where `shopping_mall_order_item_id` equals `{itemId}` and `status` is `pending` or `approved`, and `deleted_at` is null. If any such record exists, respond with 409 (conflict) indicating a refund request is already in progress for this item.

**Reason Validation**: Validate that the `reason` field in the request body is present, a non-empty string, and not whitespace-only. Reject with 422 if the reason is missing or invalid.

**Record Creation**: Insert a new row into `shopping_mall_refund_requests` with:
- `id`: generated UUID
- `shopping_mall_order_item_id`: from `{itemId}` path parameter
- `reason`: from request body
- `status`: set to `pending`
- `responded_at`: set to null (not yet responded)
- `created_at`: current timestamp
- `updated_at`: current timestamp
- `deleted_at`: null

Execute within a transaction to ensure atomicity.

**Response**: Return the created refund request with all fields populated, including the generated `id`, `status` as `pending`, `reason`, `created_at`, `updated_at`, and `responded_at` as null.

responseBody.description: The created refund request record with its generated identifier, pending status, and timestamps. The `responded_at` field is null until the seller approves or rejects the request.

parameters.description: The unique identifier of the order item for which the refund is being requested. The order item must be in `delivered` status and owned by the authenticated customer.
parameters.name: itemId

requestBody.description: The refund request payload containing the customer's reason for seeking a refund. The reason must be a non-empty string explaining why the customer wants to return the item.

prerequisites.description: Order must be placed to create the order item referenced by {itemId}. Order items are created as part of order placement — the refund request requires a target order item to exist in 'delivered' status, which is only possible after an order has been placed.

operations.description:
Retrieves a paginated list of refund requests with search and filtering capabilities.

The response is scoped to the authenticated actor: customers see only their own refund requests, sellers see only refund requests targeting items from their products, and administrators can view all refund requests across the platform.

**Filtering**

Refund requests can be filtered by status — pending (awaiting seller review), approved (seller accepted the refund), or rejected (seller declined the refund). Date range filters are available for both the submission timestamp and the seller response timestamp, enabling queries such as "all pending requests from the last 7 days" or "all approved requests responded to this month."

**Search**

Free-text search against the customer-provided reason text allows finding requests by keywords in the customer's explanation. Results are ordered by relevance when search is active, or by newest-first when browsing without search.

**Pagination**

Results are paginated to handle large volumes efficiently. Each page includes metadata indicating whether more results are available.
operations.name: index
operations.specification:
Query the shopping_mall_refund_requests table with pagination, filtering, and search capabilities. Apply data ownership isolation based on the authenticated actor:

- **Customer**: Join through shopping_mall_order_items → shopping_mall_orders and filter by shopping_mall_customer_id matching the authenticated customer. Customers can only see refund requests they submitted.

- **Seller**: Join through shopping_mall_order_items → shopping_mall_product_variants → shopping_mall_products and filter by the seller's ID. Sellers can only see refund requests targeting items from their products.

- **Administrator**: No ownership filter — administrators can view all refund requests across the platform.

Support filtering by status (single value from pending/approved/rejected), date range on created_at (request submission window), and date range on responded_at (seller response window). Support free-text search against the reason column using trigram similarity (leveraging the GIN index on reason).

Return cursor-based or offset-based pagination with configurable page size. Sort results by created_at descending (newest first) by default, with optional sort by responded_at or status.

Exclude soft-deleted records (deleted_at IS NOT NULL) from results unless the request specifies otherwise for administrative audit purposes.

Include in the summary response: refund request ID, order item reference, current status, reason preview (truncated), created_at, and responded_at (if the seller has responded). Do NOT include full reason text in the summary — full text is retrieved via the detail endpoint.

responseBody.description: Paginated list of refund request summary records, each containing the request ID, order item reference, current status, a truncated reason preview, and relevant timestamps.

requestBody.description: Search criteria for refund requests including status filter, date range filters for submission and response timestamps, free-text search against reason, and pagination parameters.

operations.description:
Respond to a pending refund request by approving or rejecting it.

A seller reviews a customer's refund request for a delivered order item and makes a decision. The response is final — once approved or rejected, the refund request cannot be changed. An immutable snapshot of the decision is created automatically for audit and dispute resolution purposes.

When approved, the system processes the refund for that item, updates the order item status to "refunded", and restores the variant's stock by creating a positive inventory record. The remaining items in the order continue processing independently.

When rejected, the order item remains in "delivered" status with no further action taken. The customer may submit a new refund request within the remaining 7-day eligibility window.
operations.name: update
operations.specification:
Validate the refund request identified by {requestId} exists and is in "pending" status. Reject with 409 Conflict if already responded to (approved/rejected) or soft-deleted.

Authorize that the calling seller owns the order item — trace through shopping_mall_order_items → shopping_mall_product_variants → shopping_mall_products → shopping_mall_seller_profiles → seller_id. Reject with 403 Forbidden if the seller does not own the item.

Accept request body with status field set to "approved" or "rejected". Reject with 400 Bad Request for any other value.

On "approved":
1. Update refund request: status = "approved", responded_at = now(), updated_at = now()
2. Update associated order item: status = "refunded", updated_at = now()
3. Create a positive inventory record for the order item's variant: quantity_change = +order_item.quantity, reason = "Refund approved for refund request {requestId}"
4. Create a refund_request_snapshot: capturing reason, status = "approved", seller_id, created_at = now()
5. After commit, recalculate parent order's derived status

On "rejected":
1. Update refund request: status = "rejected", responded_at = now(), updated_at = now()
2. LEAVE order item status as "delivered" — no change
3. Create a refund_request_snapshot: capturing reason, status = "rejected", seller_id, created_at = now()

All operations within the approval or rejection path MUST succeed or fail atomically — use a database transaction. The snapshot creation MUST never fail independently of the status update.

Edge cases:
- If the order item is no longer in "delivered" status (e.g., administrator already force-refunded), reject with 409 Conflict
- If the 7-day refund window has expired, the creation endpoint prevents new requests; this endpoint does not re-validate the window at response time
- Administrators may also use force-refund endpoints; this endpoint is specifically for seller response

responseBody.description: The refund request with its updated status, responded_at timestamp, and all associated data confirming the seller's decision has been recorded.

parameters.description: The unique identifier of the refund request to respond to.

operations.description:
Retrieves the product snapshot captured at the time of order placement for a specific order item.

This snapshot preserves the exact state of the purchased product — including its name, description, category, base price, and all gallery images with their display order — as they appeared when the customer placed the order. The data is permanently frozen and never changes, providing an authoritative historical record even if the seller later modifies or deletes the original product.

The response includes all product snapshot images captured at purchase time, preserving the gallery arrangement the customer saw. If the original product or category has been deleted since the order was placed, the snapshot data remains intact and the denormalized fields (name, description, base_price, category_name) continue to serve accurate historical information.

Access is scoped to the authenticated user's role: customers can view snapshots for their own order items, sellers can view snapshots for order items containing their products, and administrators can view any product snapshot.
operations.name: at
operations.specification:
Query the shopping_mall_order_item_product_snapshots table using the itemId path parameter, matching against shopping_mall_order_item_id (unique constraint ensures at most one record).

Include the related shopping_mall_order_item_product_snapshot_images via the productSnapshotImages HAS relation, ordered by display_order ascending to preserve the gallery arrangement as it appeared at purchase time.

Authorization:
- Customer: verify the order item belongs to an order owned by the authenticated customer (join through shopping_mall_order_items → shopping_mall_orders → shopping_mall_customer_id).
- Seller: verify the order item's product variant belongs to a product owned by the authenticated seller (join through shopping_mall_order_items → shopping_mall_product_variants → shopping_mall_products → shopping_mall_seller_profile_id → shopping_mall_seller_profiles → shopping_mall_user_id).
- Admin: no ownership restriction — can access any product snapshot.

Edge cases:

operations.description:
Retrieves the variant snapshot associated with a specific order item.

Each order item captures a variant snapshot at the moment of order placement, preserving the exact SKU code, option values, and unit price as they existed at purchase time. This snapshot is immutable — it reflects what the customer actually purchased regardless of later changes to the original product variant by the seller.

**Data Included**

The response includes the variant SKU code (the unique product identifier within the seller's catalog), the option values as a human-readable description (e.g., "Color: Red, Size: Large"), and the frozen unit price. A timestamp records when the snapshot was created, which coincides with order placement.

**Immutability**

Variant snapshots are permanently immutable. No actor — including customers, sellers, administrators, or super administrators — can modify or delete a snapshot. This guarantees that order history remains accurate and auditable for financial reconciliation and dispute resolution.

**Accessibility**

This snapshot is accessible to the customer who owns the order, the seller whose product was purchased, and platform administrators for oversight purposes.

- Return 404 if the order item exists but no variant snapshot is associated (should not occur under normal conditions, as snapshots are created atomically with order placement per section 288)

operations.description:
Lists all product images captured in the product snapshot of a specific order item.

When an order is placed, a product snapshot is created for each order item, freezing the product's state — including all images and their display order — at the moment of purchase. This endpoint retrieves those frozen images, providing an authoritative historical record of what the product listing looked like when the customer placed the order.

Each image includes its URL and display order position as it existed at purchase time. Images are sorted by their original display order by default, replicating the gallery arrangement the customer saw.

The product snapshot images are immutable — they are created once at order time and never modified. Even if the seller later deletes or replaces product images, these snapshot references remain intact for audit and dispute resolution purposes.
operations.name: index
operations.specification:
List images belonging to the product snapshot of a given order item.

**Database Query**:
1. Resolve the order item by {itemId} from shopping_mall_order_items.
2. Resolve the product snapshot via the unique constraint on shopping_mall_order_item_id — there is exactly one product snapshot per order item.
3. Query shopping_mall_order_item_product_snapshot_images filtered by the resolved snapshot ID.

**Pagination**: Cursor-based pagination using created_at as the cursor. Default page size: 20. Maximum: 100.

**Sorting**: Results sorted by display_order ascending by default (replicates the gallery order as seen at purchase time). Alternative sort by created_at descending is supported.

**Authorization**:
- Customers: can only access images for order items belonging to their own orders.
- Sellers: can only access images for order items where the product belongs to them.
- Administrators: can access images for any order item.

**Response**: Returns IPageIShoppingMallOrderItemProductSnapshotImage.ISummary with image ID, URL, display order, and creation timestamp.

**Error Handling**:
- 404 if the order item does not exist.
- 404 if no product snapshot exists for the order item (should not occur in normal operation — snapshots are created atomically at order time).
- 403 if the requester lacks authorization to view this order item.

operations.description:
Retrieves paginated audit trail of snapshots created when a seller responded to a specific cancellation request.

Each snapshot captures the exact state of the cancellation request at the moment of the seller's decision — preserving the customer's reason text and the resulting status (approved or rejected) as a permanent, immutable record. These snapshots serve as an auditable history for dispute resolution and seller accountability.

Snapshots are system-generated and cannot be created, modified, or deleted through any API. A new snapshot is automatically created each time the seller responds to the cancellation request. This endpoint provides the only read access to this historical record.

Results are paginated and sorted with the most recent snapshot first, reflecting the chronological order of seller responses to the cancellation request.
operations.name: index
operations.specification:
Query the shopping_mall_cancellation_request_snapshots table filtered by the cancellation request ID from the path parameter.

Implementation:
- Verify the cancellation request exists in shopping_mall_cancellation_requests by id = {requestId}. If not found, return 404.
- Filter snapshots WHERE shopping_mall_cancellation_request_id = {requestId}.
- Default sort by created_at descending (newest snapshot first), matching the composite index on [shopping_mall_cancellation_request_id, created_at].
- Support pagination via request body (cursor-based or offset-based).
- Support optional filtering by status ("approved" / "rejected") and created_at date range.

Access to these snapshots is restricted to the customer who submitted the cancellation request, the seller whose product is involved, and platform administrators. Unauthorized access attempts are rejected with a 403 Forbidden response.
operations.name: index
operations.specification:
Query the shopping_mall_cancellation_request_snapshots table filtered by shopping_mall_cancellation_request_id matching the {requestId} path parameter.

Access control — verify the authenticated actor is one of:
- The customer who submitted the cancellation request. Resolve by joining: shopping_mall_cancellation_requests → shopping_mall_order_items → shopping_mall_orders (check shopping_mall_customer_id against the authenticated customer's ID).
- The seller who owns the product being cancelled. Resolve by joining: shopping_mall_cancellation_requests → shopping_mall_order_items → shopping_mall_product_variants → shopping_mall_products → shopping_mall_seller_profiles → shopping_mall_sellers (check the seller's authenticated ID).
- An administrator (any grade). Bypass all ownership checks.

Reject with 403 Forbidden if the authenticated actor is none of the above.

Snapshots are immutable per business rules (sections 448, 571) — no create, update, or delete logic applies. This endpoint is strictly read-only.

Return 404 Not Found if the cancellation request referenced by {requestId} does not exist or has been soft-deleted (deleted_at IS NOT NULL).

Apply pagination from the request body (page number, items per page with a sensible default and maximum). Support sorting by created_at (newest first by default, allow ascending option via sort direction parameter). Each snapshot record includes its id, reason, status, and created_at fields.

The result set for a single cancellation request typically contains one snapshot (representing the seller's single response), but pagination is included for consistency with platform conventions.

responseBody.description: Paginated list of cancellation request snapshot summary records. Each entry contains the snapshot ID, the preserved reason text, the status at the time of capture, and the creation timestamp.

parameters.description: UUID of the cancellation request whose snapshots are being retrieved. (global scope)
parameters.name: requestId

requestBody.description: Pagination and sorting parameters for listing snapshots. Supports page number, items per page, and sort direction by creation timestamp.

prerequisites.description: Cancellation request must exist before its snapshots can be listed. The target operation returns 404 if the cancellation request referenced by {requestId} does not exist or is soft-deleted.

operations.description:
Retrieves a paginated list of immutable snapshots captured for a specific refund request.

Each snapshot preserves the exact state of the refund request at the moment a seller responded — including the customer's reason text, the resulting status (approved or rejected), the identity of the responding seller, and the timestamp of the decision. These records serve as an auditable, verifiable history for dispute resolution and regulatory compliance.

Snapshots are created automatically by the system when a seller approves or rejects a refund request. They are permanently immutable — no user, including administrators, can modify or delete them under any circumstances. Snapshots survive independently of their parent refund request, remaining accessible even if the refund request is soft-deleted or the seller's account is later removed.
operations.name: index
operations.specification:
Query the shopping_mall_refund_request_snapshots table filtered by the refund request ID from the path parameter.

Authorization:
- Sellers: May view snapshots for refund requests related to their own products. Derive ownership through the FK chain: refund_request → order_item → order_item_variant_snapshot → product_variant → product → seller_profile → seller. Verify the authenticated seller's ID matches the product's seller ID.
- Customers: May view snapshots for refund requests they submitted. Derive ownership through: refund_request → order_item → order → customer. Verify the authenticated customer's ID matches the order's customer ID.
- Administrators: May view all snapshots for any refund request without restriction.

Implementation:
- Apply pagination from the request body (cursor-based or offset pagination).
- Order results by created_at descending (newest first) by default.
- Include the id, seller_id, reason, status, and created_at fields in each summary record.
- Exclude soft-deleted snapshots — but note that snapshots themselves use the deleted_at field from the parent refund request for visibility gating. Since snapshots are immutable and never deleted, filter out snapshots whose parent refund request has a non-null deleted_at only if the requesting user is not an administrator.
- If the refund request does not exist, return a 404 error.
- If the authenticated user is not authorized to view these snapshots, return a 403 error.

Edge cases:
- An empty result set is valid — the refund request exists but is still in pending status with no seller response yet, so no snapshots have been created.
- Snapshots persist even after the parent refund request is soft-deleted (deleted_at is non-null). Administrators may still view them; customers and sellers may view them for their own records.

responseBody.description: Paginated list of refund request snapshot summaries, each containing the snapshot identifier, captured reason text, status at the time of response, responding seller identity, and creation timestamp. Results are ordered newest first.

parameters.description: Unique identifier of the refund request whose snapshots are being retrieved. This is the UUID primary key of the shopping_mall_refund_requests record.
parameters.name: requestId

requestBody.description: Pagination parameters and optional filtering criteria for browsing refund request snapshots. Supports cursor-based or offset pagination, with results ordered by creation timestamp descending by default.

prerequisites.description: A refund request must exist before its snapshots can be listed. This POST operation creates the refund request resource identified by the {requestId} path parameter in the target listing endpoint. Without a refund request, the target operation returns 404.

operations.description:
Creates a new image record within a specific order item's product snapshot.

This endpoint adds an image URL with a display order position to the frozen product snapshot associated with a given order item. The product snapshot is captured automatically at order placement and preserves the complete product state — including all gallery images — as it existed at the time of purchase. This operation allows augmenting the snapshot's image collection for historical completeness.

Each image record includes a URL pointing to the image file and a display order integer that determines its position within the gallery. Lower display order values appear first, with the lowest value serving as the main thumbnail. The image data, once created, becomes part of the immutable snapshot and provides an authoritative reference for what the product listing looked like at purchase time.
operations.name: create
operations.specification:
Create a new record in the shopping_mall_order_item_product_snapshot_images table.

1. Validate that the order item identified by {itemId} exists in shopping_mall_order_items.
2. Retrieve the associated product snapshot from shopping_mall_order_item_product_snapshots using the unique constraint on shopping_mall_order_item_id. Return 404 if no snapshot exists for this order item.
3. Generate a new UUID for the image record's id.
4. Insert a row into shopping_mall_order_item_product_snapshot_images with:
   - id: server-generated UUID
   - shopping_mall_order_item_product_snapshot_id: the snapshot's id from step 2
   - image_url: from the request body
   - display_order: from the request body
   - created_at: current timestamp
5. Return the newly created record with all fields populated.

Validation:
- image_url must be a non-empty valid URL string
- display_order must be a non-negative integer
- The requesting actor must be authorized to access this order item's snapshot

responseBody.description: The newly created product snapshot image record with all fields populated, including the server-generated id and created_at timestamp.

parameters.description: UUID of the order item whose product snapshot will receive the new image. The order item must exist and must have an associated product snapshot (created at order placement time).
parameters.name: itemId

requestBody.description: Data for the new product snapshot image. Includes the image URL and its display order position within the snapshot's gallery.

prerequisites.description: An order must be placed to create the order item and its associated product snapshot. The product snapshot is captured automatically at order placement time and must exist before snapshot images can be added.

operations.description:
Retrieves a paginated list of reviews for a specific product, ordered by newest first.

This endpoint powers the review section on the product detail page. It returns all non-deleted reviews written by verified purchasers, including the star rating, optional text content, reviewer identity, and the date each review was written.

Only active (non-deleted) reviews are returned. Reviews that have been soft-deleted by their authors are excluded from the results, from the average rating calculation, and from the total review count. When a customer who wrote a review later deletes their account, the review content and rating are preserved but the author is shown as a 'deleted user'.

The response includes pagination metadata and the total count of non-deleted reviews, enabling clients to display the average rating and review count alongside the review list on the product detail page.
operations.name: index
operations.specification:
Query the shopping_mall_review_reviews table filtered by shopping_mall_product_id matching the provided productId path parameter.

Filtering rules:
- Exclude soft-deleted reviews: WHERE deleted_at IS NULL.
- If a rating filter is provided in the request body, additionally filter WHERE rating = [requested rating value].

Sorting:
- Always sort by created_at DESC (newest first), matching the index on (shopping_mall_product_id, created_at) for optimal query performance.

Pagination:
- Support cursor-based or offset-based pagination as specified in the IRequest DTO.
- Return total count of non-deleted reviews for the product to enable client-side average rating and review count display.

Deletion handling:
- Reviews where deleted_at IS NOT NULL are excluded from results entirely.
- When the authoring customer has deleted their account, the review content and rating are preserved but the author attribution should be displayed as a 'deleted user' indicator in the ISummary response.

responseBody.description: Paginated list of review summaries for the specified product. Each summary includes the rating, content preview, reviewer display name, and creation date. Sorted newest first.

parameters.description: Unique identifier of the product whose reviews are being retrieved.
parameters.name: productId

requestBody.description: Pagination parameters and an optional rating filter to narrow results to reviews with a specific star rating (1–5).

operations.description:
Retrieves a single product review by its unique identifier.

Returns the complete review details including the star rating (1-5), optional written content, author information, and creation/update timestamps. The review must belong to the specified product — if the review ID does not correspond to a review for that product, a 404 error is returned.

Soft-deleted reviews are not visible through this endpoint. Customers who deleted their accounts will have their reviews preserved but shown as authored by a "deleted user". This endpoint supports both the product detail page (linking to individual reviews) and the review management flow where customers retrieve their own reviews before editing or deleting them.
operations.name: at
operations.specification:
Retrieve a single review from the shopping_mall_review_reviews table by its primary key (id = reviewId). Verify that the review's shopping_mall_product_id matches the productId path parameter — if it does not match, return a 404 Not Found error to maintain the RESTful resource hierarchy.

For customer and guest actors, exclude soft-deleted reviews: if the review's deleted_at is not null, return 404 Not Found. Administrator actors may retrieve soft-deleted reviews for audit purposes.

When the reviewing customer has deleted their account, the customer relationship (shopping_mall_customer_id) will no longer resolve to an active customer record. In this case, attribute the review to a "deleted user" designation in the response rather than omitting the author information.

Join with shopping_mall_customers to resolve the reviewer's display name. If the customer record no longer exists (account deleted), show the author as "deleted user".

Return 404 if no review exists with the given id, regardless of whether the id is valid UUID format.

responseBody.description: The complete review record including rating, optional text content, author attribution, and timestamps. For reviews by deleted customers, the author is shown as "deleted user".

parameters.description: Unique identifier of the product the review belongs to. Must match the shopping_mall_product_id of the target review.
parameters.name: productId

parameters.description: Unique identifier of the review to retrieve. This is the primary key of the shopping_mall_review_reviews record.
parameters.name: reviewId

prerequisites.description: The product must exist before any review can be associated with it. The target operation validates that the review's product ID matches the productId path parameter, requiring the product resource to exist in the database.

The review must be created before it can be retrieved by its ID. The target operation fetches a review by its primary key — without a prior review creation, the resource does not exist and the operation returns 404.

operations.description:
Create a new product review.

Allows an authenticated customer to write a review for a product they have purchased and received. The customer must have an order containing the product, and the corresponding order item must be in delivered status before a review can be written. Only one review per product per order is permitted — if the customer purchases the same product across multiple orders, a separate review may be written for each order.

The review requires a star rating from 1 to 5 and supports optional text content for written feedback. Once created, the review appears on the product detail page sorted by newest first and contributes to the product's average rating calculation.

Customers can later edit or delete their own reviews. Edits create immutable snapshots preserving the review history, and deleted reviews are excluded from public display and average rating calculations while their data is preserved for audit purposes.
operations.name: create
operations.specification:
Create a new product review for the authenticated customer.

**Authentication**: Requires a valid customer session. The customer ID is extracted from the session token.

**Eligibility Validation** (execute in order, return 422 with descriptive message on failure):
1. Verify the order (shopping_mall_order_id) belongs to the authenticated customer.
2. Verify the order item (shopping_mall_order_item_id) belongs to the order and references the product (shopping_mall_product_id).
3. Verify the order item status is 'delivered' — reviews can only be written after the item has been delivered.
4. Check the unique constraint: query shopping_mall_review_reviews for an existing non-deleted review with the same (customer_id, product_id, order_id). If found, return 409 Conflict.

**Creation**:
- Insert a new row into shopping_mall_review_reviews with: id (generated UUID), shopping_mall_customer_id (from session), shopping_mall_product_id, shopping_mall_order_id, shopping_mall_order_item_id, rating (1-5), content (nullable string), created_at (now), updated_at (now), deleted_at (null).

**Response**: Return the created review as IShoppingMallReviewReview with all fields populated. Join with customer to include display_name for the reviewer identity.

**Error cases**:
- 401 Unauthorized: No valid customer session.
- 422 Unprocessable Entity: Invalid eligibility (wrong customer, wrong product-order_item association, item not delivered).
- 409 Conflict: Review already exists for this customer-product-order combination.
- 400 Bad Request: Rating outside 1-5 range or missing required fields.

responseBody.description: The newly created review with all fields populated, including the reviewer's display name.

requestBody.description: Review creation payload containing the product and order references, star rating, and optional text content. The customer identity is derived from the authenticated session.

prerequisites.description: The product being reviewed must exist in the catalog. The review's shopping_mall_product_id FK references shopping_mall_products, so the product must be created first.

The order item referenced by shopping_mall_order_item_id in turn references a product variant via shopping_mall_product_variant_id. At least one variant must exist for the product before an order item can reference it.

The order (shopping_mall_order_id) and its order items (shopping_mall_order_item_id) are created atomically during checkout. The review references both, so the order must be placed — creating the order and its items — before a review can be written.

operations.description:
Search and list product reviews across the platform with flexible filtering, sorting, and pagination.

Reviews capture verified-purchase customer feedback. Each review contains a required 1-to-5-star rating and optional written content. Only customers who purchased and received a product can write reviews, ensuring authentic feedback grounded in real product experience.

**Filtering capabilities**: Narrow results by specific product, customer, order, or order item. Filter by rating range to surface highly-rated or critical reviews. Search review content for specific terms or phrases. Date range filters support browsing reviews from a particular time period.

**Default visibility**: Soft-deleted reviews are excluded from results by default, consistent with their removal from product detail pages and exclusion from average rating calculations. An administrative override allows including deleted reviews for moderation and audit purposes.

**Sorting**: Results are sorted newest first by default, matching the display order on product detail pages. Alternative sorting by rating or most-recently-edited is supported.

**Account deletion preservation**: Reviews written by customers who later deleted their accounts are preserved with intact content and rating. The reviewer is displayed as 'deleted user' while the original feedback remains available for product evaluation.
operations.name: index
operations.specification:
Query the shopping_mall_review_reviews table with cursor-based pagination, flexible filtering, and configurable sorting.

**Default soft-delete behavior**: Filter WHERE deleted_at IS NULL by default, excluding soft-deleted reviews from results. This mirrors the product detail page behavior where deleted reviews are hidden from public view and excluded from average rating calculations. Accept an optional includeDeleted boolean in the request body; when true, bypass the soft-delete filter to include deleted reviews for administrative moderation and audit workflows.

**Filtering**: Apply optional equality filters on shopping_mall_customer_id, shopping_mall_product_id, shopping_mall_order_id, and shopping_mall_order_item_id. Support rating range filtering via ratingMin and ratingMax (inclusive, 1 to 5). Support created_at range filtering via createdFrom and createdTo. Support updated_at range filtering via updatedFrom and updatedTo. Support content text search via contentSearch using case-insensitive partial matching (ILIKE '%term%'). Apply all provided filters conjunctively (AND).

**Sorting**: Default sort is created_at DESC (newest first), matching the product detail page display order defined in requirements. Support alternative sort fields via sortField: 'created_at' (default), 'rating', 'updated_at'. Support sort direction via sortDirection: 'asc' or 'desc' (default).

**Pagination**: Use cursor-based pagination with cursor (the value of the sort field from the last item of the previous page) and limit (default 20, maximum 100). Return totalCount for the total number of matching records to enable UI page count display.

**Deleted user handling**: When a review's author has deleted their account, the response SHALL display the reviewer as 'deleted user' rather than the original display name, preserving the review content and rating per the account deletion preservation rule.

**Access control**: Authenticated users only — guests are denied. Customers can query their own reviews by filtering on their customer_id. Sellers can filter reviews for their products. Administrators have unrestricted access including the includeDeleted override.

responseBody.description: Paginated list of review summary records. Each entry includes the rating, a content preview, reviewer display name (or 'deleted user' for deleted accounts), product reference, and creation date. Soft-deleted reviews are excluded by default.

requestBody.description: Search criteria for filtering, sorting, and paginating reviews. Supports optional filters by product, customer, order, order item, rating range, content text search, date ranges, and a soft-delete inclusion toggle for administrators.

operations.description:
Retrieves a single review by its unique identifier.

Returns the full review record including the star rating (1–5), optional written feedback text, the author's customer ID, the reviewed product ID, and the order context linking the review to a verified purchase. The response includes creation and modification timestamps, as well as the soft-delete timestamp when applicable.

Reviews are tied to verified purchases: a customer may only write a review after the corresponding order item reaches delivered status. One review is permitted per product per order, enforced by a database-level uniqueness constraint.
operations.name: at
operations.specification:
Query the shopping_mall_review_reviews table by primary key (id = reviewId).

Return the full review entity including:
- id, rating, content, created_at, updated_at, deleted_at
- shopping_mall_customer_id (author reference)
- shopping_mall_product_id (reviewed product)
- shopping_mall_order_id and shopping_mall_order_item_id (purchase context)

Include soft-deleted reviews in the result — the deleted_at field indicates deletion status. Consumers (e.g., product detail page) are responsible for filtering out soft-deleted reviews where appropriate.

If no review exists with the given ID, return a 404 error.

responseBody.description: The full review entity with rating, content, author and product references, purchase context, and all timestamps including soft-delete status.

parameters.description: Unique identifier of the review to retrieve. UUID format.
parameters.name: reviewId

operations.description:
Edits an existing review written by the authenticated customer.

This endpoint allows a customer to update the star rating, the written feedback, or both on a review they previously authored. The review must belong to the authenticated customer and must not have been previously deleted.

When a review is edited, the system automatically preserves the previous state by creating an immutable snapshot that records the rating and text content as they were before the change. This ensures a complete and auditable history of all modifications to every review.

The review's original creation date is never altered. This means the review retains its position in the newest-first display order on the product detail page regardless of how many times it is edited. The product's average rating is recalculated after the update to reflect the new rating value.
operations.name: update
operations.specification:
Update a review owned by the authenticated customer. The implementation must:

1. Authenticate: Verify the requester is a customer. Reject with 401 if unauthenticated or not a customer.

2. Retrieve the review: Query shopping_mall_review_reviews by reviewId. Reject with 404 if the review does not exist or if deleted_at is not null (soft-deleted reviews cannot be edited).

3. Ownership check: Verify that shopping_mall_customer_id matches the authenticated customer's ID. Reject with 403 if the review belongs to a different customer.

4. Validate input: Ensure rating is an integer between 1 and 5 inclusive. Reject with 400 if rating is missing, out of range, or non-integer. Content is optional — null is accepted and means the review has no text.

5. Create snapshot (before update): Insert a row into shopping_mall_review_review_snapshots with shopping_mall_review_review_id set to reviewId, rating set to the current (pre-edit) rating value, content set to the current (pre-edit) content value, and created_at set to the current timestamp. This preserves the audit trail.

6. Apply update: Set rating to the new value, content to the new value (may be null), and updated_at to the current timestamp. Do NOT modify created_at, id, shopping_mall_customer_id, shopping_mall_product_id, shopping_mall_order_id, shopping_mall_order_item_id, or deleted_at.

7. Return the fully updated review entity including all fields.

Edge cases:
- If the new rating and content are identical to the existing values, the snapshot is still created and updated_at is still refreshed — this maintains audit consistency and signals that an edit action was performed even if values didn't change.
- The review's position in product detail page listings (sorted by created_at descending per the @@index([shopping_mall_product_id, created_at])) does not change after edit.
- The product's average rating must be recalculated from all non-deleted reviews after the rating change.

responseBody.description: The fully updated review entity reflecting the new rating, content, and updated_at timestamp. Includes all associated identifiers (customer, product, order, order item) and timestamps.

parameters.description: Unique identifier of the review to update. Must be a valid UUID referencing an existing, non-deleted review owned by the authenticated customer.
parameters.name: reviewId

requestBody.description: The updated review data containing the new star rating (integer from 1 to 5) and optional text content. Content may be null to indicate a rating-only review.

prerequisites.description: The review must be created before it can be edited. POST /shoppingMall/customer/reviews creates the review entity that this PUT operation modifies.

operations.description:
Soft-deletes a review written by the authenticated customer.

When a review is deleted, it is immediately hidden from the product detail page. Its star rating is excluded from the product's average rating calculation, and the total review count displayed on the product page is decremented accordingly. Other customers will no longer see this review when browsing the product.

The review data — including the star rating, text content, and creation timestamp — is preserved in the database for audit and dispute resolution. All snapshots associated with the review (created during previous edits via `shopping_mall_review_review_snapshots`) remain available for historical record-keeping even after the review itself is deleted.

Only the review author may delete their own review. If the authenticated customer is not the original author, the operation is rejected with a 403 Forbidden response. An already-deleted review cannot be deleted again — attempting to do so returns a 409 Conflict.
operations.name: erase
operations.specification:
Soft-delete a review by setting its `deleted_at` timestamp to NOW(). The `updated_at` field is also refreshed to NOW().

**Authorization**:
Compare the authenticated customer ID against the review's `shopping_mall_customer_id`. Reject with 403 Forbidden if the authenticated customer is not the review author.

**Database Operations**:
1. Query `shopping_mall_review_reviews` by `id` matching the `{reviewId}` path parameter. Return 404 Not Found if no matching record exists.
2. Compare the authenticated customer ID against `shopping_mall_customer_id`. Return 403 Forbidden on mismatch.
3. Check `deleted_at`: if already non-null, return 409 Conflict — the review has already been deleted (idempotency guard).
4. Update the record: SET `deleted_at = NOW()`, `updated_at = NOW()`.
5. Return the updated review entity including the new `deleted_at` timestamp.

**Side Effects**:
- The review is excluded from product detail page display.
- The review's rating is excluded from the product's average rating calculation.
- The review is excluded from the total review count.
- All associated `shopping_mall_review_review_snapshots` records are preserved unchanged.

**Edge Cases**:
- Idempotency: attempting to delete an already-deleted review returns 409 Conflict rather than silently succeeding.
- Deleted user scenario: If the customer account that authored the review has been deleted, the review displays as authored by "deleted user" and this deletion operation is no longer possible since the customer account no longer exists.
- Soft-delete does NOT cascade: references to product, order, and order-item remain intact.

parameters.description: The unique identifier of the review to delete, in UUID format. This corresponds to the primary key of the `shopping_mall_review_reviews` table.
parameters.name: reviewId

prerequisites.description: The review must exist before it can be soft-deleted. This POST operation creates the review entity identified by {reviewId}, including all required associations — customer (author), product (review target), order (purchase context), and order-item (delivered status verification).

operations.description:
Retrieves the edit history of a review.

Each snapshot records the state of a review before an edit was applied, capturing the previous rating and text content along with the timestamp of the change. Together they form a complete chronological audit trail showing how the review evolved over time.

Snapshots are created automatically whenever a customer edits their own review. They are permanently immutable — no actor or process can modify or delete them. Even when the parent review is deleted by the customer or the authoring customer removes their account, the snapshots remain preserved and accessible to administrators for dispute resolution and record-keeping purposes.
operations.name: index
operations.specification:
Query shopping_mall_review_review_snapshots filtered by the parent review ID from the path parameter.

Authorization:
- Customers: must own the review (shopping_mall_customer_id matches the authenticated customer). Verify the review exists and belongs to the requesting customer before querying snapshots. If the review does not exist or does not belong to the customer, reject with an appropriate error.
- Administrators: may view snapshots of any review without ownership restriction.

Query logic:
- Filter by shopping_mall_review_review_id = {reviewId}.
- Apply optional date range filters on created_at if provided in the request body.
- Apply optional rating range filters (snapshot's captured rating) if provided.
- Support cursor-based or offset pagination.
- Order by created_at descending (newest snapshot first).

Snapshots are permanently immutable — never allow modification or deletion of snapshot records under any circumstance. This endpoint is strictly read-only.

responseBody.description: Paginated list of review snapshot summary records, each containing the captured rating, content, and creation timestamp of the snapshot at the moment the review was edited.

parameters.description: The unique identifier of the review whose snapshot edit history is being retrieved. (global scope)
parameters.name: reviewId

requestBody.description: Search and pagination criteria for filtering review snapshots. Supports filtering by created_at date range and rating range to narrow down the edit history.

prerequisites.description: A review must exist before its snapshot edit history can be retrieved. The review is referenced by the reviewId path parameter, and the specification requires verifying the review exists before querying its snapshots.

operations.description:
Retrieves the edit history of a review.

Each snapshot records the state of a review before an edit was applied, capturing the previous rating and text content along with the timestamp of the change. Together they form a complete chronological audit trail showing how the review evolved over time.

Snapshots are created automatically whenever a customer edits their own review. They are permanently immutable — no actor or process can modify or delete them. Even when the parent review is deleted by the customer or the authoring customer removes their account, the snapshots remain preserved and accessible to administrators for dispute resolution and record-keeping purposes.
operations.name: index
operations.specification:
Query shopping_mall_review_review_snapshots filtered by the parent review ID from the path parameter.

Authorization:
- Customers: must own the review (shopping_mall_customer_id matches the authenticated customer). Verify the review exists and belongs to the requesting customer before querying snapshots. If the review does not exist or does not belong to the customer, reject with an appropriate error.
- Administrators: may view snapshots of any review without ownership restriction.

Query logic:
- Filter by shopping_mall_review_review_id = {reviewId}.
- Apply optional date range filters on created_at if provided in the request body.
- Apply optional rating range filters (snapshot's captured rating) if provided.
- Support cursor-based or offset pagination.
- Order by created_at descending (newest snapshot first).

Snapshots are permanently immutable — never allow modification or deletion of snapshot records under any circumstance. This endpoint is strictly read-only.

responseBody.description: Paginated list of review snapshot summary records, each containing the captured rating, content, and creation timestamp of the snapshot at the moment the review was edited.

parameters.description: The unique identifier of the review whose snapshot edit history is being retrieved. (global scope)
parameters.name: reviewId

requestBody.description: Search and pagination criteria for filtering review snapshots. Supports filtering by created_at date range and rating range to narrow down the edit history.

operations.description:
Retrieves a single immutable snapshot of a review's previous state.

When a customer edits their review, the system automatically creates a snapshot capturing the rating and text content as they were before the edit took effect. This endpoint returns that frozen record, identified by the snapshot's unique ID within the context of its parent review.

Snapshots are preserved indefinitely and cannot be modified or deleted by any actor — including the customer who wrote the review, the seller of the product, administrators, and super administrators. They remain accessible even after the parent review is soft-deleted or the authoring customer removes their account, ensuring a complete and tamper-proof audit trail for dispute resolution and historical reference.
operations.name: at
operations.specification:
Query the shopping_mall_review_review_snapshots table where id equals the snapshotId parameter AND shopping_mall_review_review_id equals the reviewId parameter.

Verify that the parent review exists in the shopping_mall_review_reviews table — the snapshot should be retrievable even if the parent review has been soft-deleted (deleted_at is set), as snapshots are preserved indefinitely for audit purposes per the snapshot immutability rules.

Return the full snapshot entity including: id (UUID primary key), rating (the star rating value from 1 to 5 that was in place before the edit), content (the text content before the edit, nullable — null when the review had no text), and created_at (the timestamp when the snapshot was created, corresponding to the exact moment the review edit occurred).

If no snapshot exists with the given snapshotId under the given reviewId, return a 404 Not Found response.

Snapshots are immutable — this endpoint is strictly read-only. No write operations (POST, PUT, PATCH, DELETE) are permitted on snapshots. No actor can edit or delete snapshots under any circumstance.

responseBody.description: The full review snapshot entity containing the preserved rating, text content, and creation timestamp at the moment the review was edited.

The snapshot is scoped under the review via the shopping_mall_review_review_id foreign key — without an existing review record, the snapshot query context is invalid.

operations.description:
Retrieves a single immutable snapshot of a review's previous state.

When a customer edits their review, the system automatically creates a snapshot capturing the rating and text content as they were before the edit took effect. This endpoint returns that frozen record, identified by the snapshot's unique ID within the context of its parent review.

Snapshots are preserved indefinitely and cannot be modified or deleted by any actor — including the customer who wrote the review, the seller of the product, administrators, and super administrators. They remain accessible even after the parent review is soft-deleted or the authoring customer removes their account, ensuring a complete and tamper-proof audit trail for dispute resolution and historical reference.
