id.description:
Unique identifier for the customer account.

A UUID v4 string that uniquely identifies this customer across the platform. Use this identifier to retrieve full customer details via the customer detail endpoint or to perform administrative actions such as ban, unban, or session review.
id.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from shopping_mall_customers.id. UUID primary key — unique identifier for the customer account.

email.description:
Customer's email address used as the login identifier.

This email is unique across all customer accounts and serves as the primary login credential. It is exposed in the summary view for administrative identification and search purposes. The email format must conform to standard email address validation.
email.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from shopping_mall_customers.email. Unique constraint across all customer accounts — serves as the login identifier.

display_name.description:
Public display name of the customer.

Shown on reviews, profile pages, and across the platform as the customer's visible identity. Set at registration and editable by the customer through profile management. This is how the customer appears to other platform users.
display_name.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from shopping_mall_customers.display_name. Set at registration and editable by the customer through profile management.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when the customer account was registered.

ISO 8601 date-time string in UTC with timezone offset indicating when this customer first joined the platform. This value is set once at registration and never changes.
created_at.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from shopping_mall_customers.created_at. ISO 8601 date-time with timezone — records when the customer account was first registered.

banned_at.description:
Timestamp when an administrator banned this customer account, or null if the account is in good standing.

A non-null value indicates the customer is currently banned and cannot log into the platform. Banned customers' existing orders and reviews remain intact. A null value indicates the account has full platform access. Administrators use the ban and unban actions to manage this field.
banned_at.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from shopping_mall_customers.banned_at. Nullable DateTime — null means the account is in good standing with full platform access. Non-null indicates the timestamp when an administrator banned this customer, preventing login.

IShoppingMallCustomer.ISummary.description:
Summary view of a customer account for administrative listing.

Contains the essential fields needed for administrators to browse and identify customer accounts: the unique identifier for detail retrieval, the login email address, the public display name, the registration timestamp, and the optional ban status indicator.

Password hashes are never exposed. Phone numbers and soft-deletion timestamps are omitted to keep summary responses lean — full details are available through the customer detail endpoint. All related entities (sessions, password resets, email verifications, wishlist items, cart items, orders, reviews) are accessible through their own dedicated endpoints.
IShoppingMallCustomer.ISummary.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from shopping_mall_customers for administrative customer listing. Maps: id, email, display_name, created_at, banned_at. Excluded: password_hash (security — never exposed), phone_number (lean summary — available via detail endpoint), updated_at (not in summary scope), deleted_at (soft-deleted customers filtered out by default). All has-many relations excluded — available via separate endpoints.

email.description:
The administrator's email address used for authentication.

Must be a valid email format and unique across all active administrator accounts on the platform. This email serves as the login identifier for the administrator and is used for all subsequent authentication operations including login and token refresh.
email.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from shopping_mall_admins.email. Must validate uniqueness across all active (non-deleted) administrator accounts. Return 409 Conflict if a duplicate active email is detected.

password.description:
The administrator's account password.

The password is transmitted as plain text and hashed by the server using a cryptographically secure one-way algorithm before storage. The raw password is never stored, logged, or returned in any response. Must meet minimum length and complexity requirements.
password.x-autobe-specification: Maps to shopping_mall_admins.password_hash via server-side cryptographic hashing (bcrypt or argon2). The raw password is never stored or logged. Must meet minimum security requirements for length and complexity before hashing.

href.description:
The full URL of the page from which the administrator is registering.

Captured from the client's current browser URL at the time of registration. This value is stored in the session record for security audit purposes and helps track the origin of administrator account creations.
href.x-autobe-specification: Session context: the full URL of the registration page. Stored in shopping_mall_admin_sessions.href for audit purposes. Used to track where the administrator registered from.

referrer.description:
The referring URL that led to the registration page.

Captured from the browser's document.referrer at the time of registration. This value is stored in the session record for security audit purposes and helps identify how the administrator reached the registration page.
referrer.x-autobe-specification: Session context: the referring URL (document.referrer). Stored in shopping_mall_admin_sessions.referrer for audit purposes.

ip.description:
The IP address of the client registering the administrator account.

Captured from the client's network connection. In server-side rendering contexts where the client cannot determine its own IP address, this field may be omitted and the server will use the actual connection IP as a fallback.
ip.x-autobe-specification: Session context: the client's IP address. Stored in shopping_mall_admin_sessions.ip. In SSR contexts, the client may not know its own IP — the server falls back to the actual connection IP (body.ip ?? serverIp) when not provided.

IShoppingMallAdmin.IJoin.description:
A registration payload for creating a new platform administrator account.

Contains the administrator's email and password credentials along with session context information. Upon successful registration, the account is assigned the 'regular' grade by default, an authenticated session is created immediately, and JWT tokens are returned — no separate login step is required.

The email must be unique across all active administrator accounts. The password is hashed server-side before storage and is never logged or returned in responses. Session context fields (href, referrer, ip) are captured for security audit purposes and stored in the administrator's session record.
IShoppingMallAdmin.IJoin.x-autobe-specification: Maps email directly to shopping_mall_admins.email with uniqueness validation against active (non-deleted) records. Maps password to shopping_mall_admins.password_hash via server-side bcrypt/argon2 hashing — raw password never persisted. Session context fields (href, referrer, ip) are stored in shopping_mall_admin_sessions for audit. Excluded from DTO: id (auto-generated UUID), grade (defaults to 'regular'), created_at/updated_at (auto timestamps), deleted_at (irrelevant for registration), and all reverse relations (adminSessions, passwordResets, auditLogs) which are created server-side.

id.description:
Unique identifier of the customer account.

A UUID v4 value assigned at registration and immutable throughout the account lifecycle. Used as the primary key for all customer-related operations and as a foreign key reference in orders, reviews, and session records.
id.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from shopping_mall_customers.id. UUID primary key, auto-generated at registration. Used as the path parameter in admin endpoints (e.g., /admin/customers/{customerId}).

email.description:
Customer's email address serving as the unique login identifier.

Must be unique across all customer accounts on the platform. Used for authentication in combination with a password, and for account-related communications such as password reset and email verification. The email is set at registration and cannot be changed through profile updates.
email.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from shopping_mall_customers.email. Unique constraint enforced at database level. Used as the login identifier — customers authenticate with email and password. Immutable after registration.

display_name.description:
Public display name shown on reviews, profile pages, and throughout the platform.

This is the customer's visible identity to other users. Set during registration and editable at any time through the profile update endpoint. The display name appears on product reviews, order records, and any public-facing content authored by the customer. When a customer deletes their account, reviews authored by them display as authored by a 'deleted user' instead of this name.
display_name.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from shopping_mall_customers.display_name. Set at registration and editable by the customer through profile update. Displayed on reviews, profile pages, and across the platform. Must be a non-empty string after trimming.

phone_number.description:
Customer's phone number for contact purposes.

An optional field that customers may provide or leave empty. Can be updated or cleared through the profile update endpoint. Used for order-related contact and shipping communications. A null value indicates the customer has not provided a phone number.
phone_number.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from shopping_mall_customers.phone_number. Nullable — customers may choose not to provide a phone number. Editable through profile update: omit to preserve, set to null to clear, or provide a string to update. No format validation beyond being a string.

banned_at.description:
Timestamp indicating when an administrator banned this customer account.

A null value means the account is in good standing and the customer can log in normally. A non-null timestamp indicates the account has been banned — the customer's credentials are rejected at authentication, preventing login. Existing orders and reviews are preserved regardless of ban status. The ban can be reversed through the unban endpoint, which clears this timestamp.
banned_at.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from shopping_mall_customers.banned_at. Nullable — null means the customer is in good standing. A non-null DateTime value indicates an administrator has banned this account, and the customer cannot log in. Set via POST /admin/customers/{customerId}/ban, cleared via POST /admin/customers/{customerId}/unban.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when the customer account was registered.

Set automatically at account creation and never modified. Represents the moment the customer completed the registration process and joined the platform.
created_at.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from shopping_mall_customers.created_at. Auto-set at registration time. Immutable — never updated after initial creation.

updated_at.description:
Timestamp of the most recent modification to any field on this customer record.

Updated automatically whenever the customer's data changes — profile edits, ban status changes, or account deletion. Provides an audit trail of when the account was last modified.
updated_at.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from shopping_mall_customers.updated_at. Auto-updated on every modification to the customer record including profile updates, ban/unban actions, and soft-deletion.

deleted_at.description:
Soft-deletion timestamp indicating when the customer voluntarily deleted their account.

A null value means the account is active. When set, the account is considered deleted — the customer's profile information is discarded but their orders and order history are preserved for seller records and legal purposes. Reviews authored by the deleted customer remain visible on product pages but are displayed as authored by a 'deleted user'. Administrators can still access deleted account records through the customer retrieval endpoint.
deleted_at.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from shopping_mall_customers.deleted_at. Nullable — null means the account is active. A non-null DateTime indicates the customer has soft-deleted their account. Profile information is discarded but orders and reviews are preserved. Reviews authored by deleted customers display as 'deleted user'. Administrators can still view deleted accounts.

IShoppingMallCustomer.description:
Full customer account details for administrative overview and customer self-profile viewing.

The account identity is established through the unique email address used at registration and serves as the login identifier across all customer accounts. The display name is the public-facing identity shown on reviews, profile pages, and throughout the platform. An optional phone number provides an additional contact channel.

Account status is tracked through three temporal markers: the ban timestamp indicates whether an administrator has restricted access — a banned customer cannot log in. The soft-deletion timestamp records when the customer voluntarily deleted their account, after which profile information is discarded while orders and reviews are preserved for legal and historical purposes. Creation and update timestamps provide audit context.

The password hash is never included in any API response for security.
IShoppingMallCustomer.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from shopping_mall_customers table. All columns except password_hash are included — password hashes must never be exposed in API responses. This is a Read DTO used by admin customer retrieval (GET /shoppingMall/admin/customers/{customerId}), customer profile view/update responses (GET /shoppingMall/seller/profile, PUT /shoppingMall/customer/profile), and ban/unban responses. Relations (sessions, passwordResets, emailVerifications, wishlistItems, cartItems, orders, reviews) are excluded — each has dedicated endpoints. Soft-deleted accounts (deleted_at IS NOT NULL) are included in query results so administrators can review deleted accounts.

refresh_token.description:
The current refresh token to be exchanged for a new JWT token pair.

This is a signed JWT issued during the guest's initial identification (join) or a previous token refresh. It contains encoded claims including the guest's unique identifier and the current session ID, which the server uses to locate and validate the existing session before issuing new tokens.

If the refresh token has expired or the associated session has passed its expiration boundary, the guest must re-establish identity through the join endpoint using their device fingerprint.
refresh_token.x-autobe-specification: JWT refresh token extracted from request body. Decoded server-side to retrieve sub (guest_id) and session_id claims. Used to query shopping_mall_guest_sessions by id = session_id for validation (session must exist, belong to guest, and not expired). Also used to query shopping_mall_guests by id = guest_id to verify guest exists and deleted_at IS NULL. On validation failure, returns 401. The token itself is never stored as-is in a database column.

href.description:
The current page URL where the guest is located at the time of token refresh.

Captured as part of the session context for security auditing and traffic pattern analysis. This value is written into the new session record created upon successful token refresh, replacing the URL from the previous session.
href.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping to shopping_mall_guest_sessions.href. Written into the newly created session row on successful token refresh. Captures the current page URL the guest is on at the time of refresh for audit and security analysis.

referrer.description:
The URL of the page that referred the guest to the current page.

Derived from the HTTP Referer header and recorded in the new session for traffic source analysis. This helps understand how guests navigate between the login and registration pages and discover the platform.
referrer.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping to shopping_mall_guest_sessions.referrer. Written into the newly created session row on successful token refresh. Captures the HTTP Referer header indicating which page led the guest to the current page.

ip.description:
The IP address of the guest client at the time of token refresh.

Recorded in the new session for security auditing and geographic access pattern analysis. This field is optional to accommodate server-side rendering (SSR) scenarios where the client's IP address may not be directly available at request time. When omitted, the server captures the connecting IP address as a fallback.
ip.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping to shopping_mall_guest_sessions.ip. Written into the newly created session row on successful token refresh. Captures the guest's IP address for security audit. Optional to support SSR contexts where the client IP may not be available at request time — the server captures it as fallback.

IShoppingMallGuest.IRefresh.description:
Token refresh payload for exchanging an existing guest refresh token for a new JWT token pair.

Guests use this endpoint when their access token expires to obtain a fresh token pair without re-identifying via device fingerprint. The refresh token embedded in the JWT identifies the current session, and on successful validation, a brand new session is created carrying forward the guest identity.

Each refresh captures updated session context — the guest's current page URL, referring page, and IP address — which is written into the new session record for audit purposes. The old session is preserved unchanged, maintaining a complete append-only audit trail of all guest sessions.
IShoppingMallGuest.IRefresh.x-autobe-specification: Request DTO for guest token refresh. refresh_token: JWT token extracted from body, decoded to retrieve sub (guest_id) and session_id claims, used to look up and validate the existing session in shopping_mall_guest_sessions. On successful validation, a new session row is INSERTed into shopping_mall_guest_sessions with href, referrer, and ip from the request body. id is auto-generated UUID, shopping_mall_guest_id is resolved from JWT sub claim, created_at is set to now(), expired_at is set to now() + session_ttl. Old session is preserved as audit trail (append-only pattern).

IShoppingMallGuest.description:
A temporary guest account created for each unauthenticated visitor to the platform.

Guests are identified by a unique device fingerprint and tracked from their first visit until they register, log in, or the account is cleaned up. This type exposes the full guest record including all associated session tokens for administrative inspection.
IShoppingMallGuest.x-autobe-specification: Direct: id, device_fingerprint, created_at, updated_at, deleted_at. Relations: sessions via HAS-MANY composition (shopping_mall_guest_sessions). deleted_at uses oneOf for null handling.

email.description:
The seller's registered email address.

Used as the primary authentication identifier alongside the password. Must match an existing seller account in the system. The comparison is case-insensitive — "Seller@Example.com" and "seller@example.com" are treated as the same email.
email.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from shopping_mall_sellers.email. Matched case-insensitively during authentication lookup. Unique constraint enforces one account per email.

password.description:
The seller's account password in plaintext.

Verified against the stored bcrypt hash during authentication. The password is never stored in plaintext — it is only used for one-time comparison and then discarded. A mismatched password results in a 401 Unauthorized response without revealing whether the email address exists.
password.x-autobe-specification: Compared against shopping_mall_sellers.password_hash using bcrypt. Never stored as plaintext — only the bcrypt hash is persisted. The plaintext password in this DTO is transient and discarded after verification.

href.description:
The full URL of the page where the seller initiated login.

Captured for session audit purposes and stored in the session record upon successful authentication. This helps trace the origin of login attempts for security monitoring.
href.x-autobe-specification: Written to shopping_mall_seller_sessions.href on successful authentication. Captures the full URL of the login page for security audit purposes. Not persisted to shopping_mall_sellers.

referrer.description:
The URL of the referring page that led the seller to the login page.

Captured for session audit purposes and stored in the session record upon successful authentication. This provides context about how the seller arrived at the login page for security analysis.
referrer.x-autobe-specification: Written to shopping_mall_seller_sessions.referrer on successful authentication. Captures the referring site URL for security audit purposes. Not persisted to shopping_mall_sellers.

ip.description:
The client's IP address at the time of login.

Optional field — in server-side rendering environments, the client may not be able to determine its own IP address. When not provided, the server captures the actual IP address from the incoming request as a fallback. Stored in the session record for security audit purposes.
ip.x-autobe-specification: Written to shopping_mall_seller_sessions.ip on successful authentication. Optional because in SSR (Server Side Rendering) the client cannot determine its own IP address. When not provided by the client, the server captures the actual IP as fallback (body.ip ?? serverIp). Not persisted to shopping_mall_sellers.

IShoppingMallSeller.ILogin.description:
Seller login credentials for authenticating into the shopping mall platform.

Contains the seller's registered email address and password for credential verification against the stored bcrypt hash in shopping_mall_sellers. Session context fields — the page URL, referring site, and optional client IP address — are included to create a session record upon successful authentication.

Banned sellers (banned_at is set) are prevented from logging in entirely with a 403 Forbidden response. Suspended sellers (suspended_at is set) can still log in — suspension only limits selling features such as product visibility and new product creation. Sellers in any approval status (pending, approved, rejected) can log in; pending and rejected sellers have limited functionality until approved.
IShoppingMallSeller.ILogin.x-autobe-specification: Credential lookup DTO for seller login authentication. email is matched case-insensitively against shopping_mall_sellers.email. password is compared against shopping_mall_sellers.password_hash using bcrypt. Session context fields (href, referrer, ip) are not persisted to shopping_mall_sellers — they are written to shopping_mall_seller_sessions on successful authentication along with seller_id, created_at, and expired_at. ip is optional because in SSR the client cannot know its own IP; the server captures it as fallback (body.ip ?? serverIp).

IShoppingMallCustomer.IJoin.description:
Customer self-registration request.

Contains the information needed to create a new customer account on the platform. The email address serves as the unique login identifier and must not already be associated with an active customer account. The password is transmitted as plain text and will be securely hashed before storage; it is never persisted in its original form.

The display name is the customer's public-facing name shown on reviews, profile pages, and across the platform. An optional phone number may be provided for contact purposes.

Session context fields (href and referrer) capture the originating page information for session creation and security auditing. The optional ip field provides the client's IP address for rate limiting when not inferable from the request context (e.g., server-side rendering scenarios).
IShoppingMallCustomer.IJoin.x-autobe-specification: Maps: email, password (→password_hash in DB), display_name, phone_number (optional). Session context: href (originating page URL), referrer, ip (optional for SSR). Excluded: id (auto UUID), banned_at (admin-managed), created_at/updated_at/deleted_at (server timestamps). Backend validates email uniqueness among non-deleted customers, hashes password with bcrypt/argon2, creates session in shopping_mall_customer_sessions, generates email verification token.

refresh.description:
JWT refresh token for obtaining a new access token without re-authentication.

The refresh token is a JSON Web Token string issued during seller login or a previous token refresh. It contains an encoded session identifier and expiration claim. Must correspond to an active session in the seller session store with a future expiration timestamp.

Must belong to a seller account that is neither banned nor soft-deleted. Should be stored securely and transmitted only to the token refresh endpoint.
refresh.x-autobe-specification: JWT refresh token issued during seller login or a previous token refresh. Not a direct database column mapping — the token encodes a session ID that links to shopping_mall_seller_sessions. Downstream: validate cryptographic signature and expiration claim, decode session ID from payload, look up session in shopping_mall_seller_sessions, verify session validity and seller account status (deleted_at IS NULL, banned_at IS NULL), generate new access token, optionally rotate refresh token.

IShoppingMallSeller.IRefresh.description:
Refresh token request for renewing an expiring seller access token.

Contains the refresh token originally issued during seller login or a previous token refresh. The token is a JWT string that encodes session information and expiration claims. When submitted to the refresh endpoint, the token is validated against the active session record in the seller session store.

If the token is valid and the associated session is not expired, a new access token is issued — and optionally a new refresh token for continued session extension. Expired or revoked refresh tokens are rejected with an authentication error.
IShoppingMallSeller.IRefresh.x-autobe-specification: Computed type with no database table mapping. The refresh token is a JWT string issued by the authentication system during seller login or a previous token refresh. It encodes a session ID and expiration claim. Downstream implementation: (1) extract the refresh token from the request body, (2) validate its cryptographic signature and expiration claim, (3) decode the session ID from the token payload, (4) look up the corresponding session in shopping_mall_seller_sessions by that session ID, (5) verify the session exists and expired_at > current timestamp, (6) verify the associated seller account is active (deleted_at IS NULL, banned_at IS NULL), (7) generate a new JWT access token bound to the same session, (8) optionally rotate the refresh token by issuing a new one and updating the session's expired_at, (9) return IShoppingMallSeller.IAuthorized containing the new token pair and seller identity. Edge cases: invalid/expired/malformed token → 401; session not found → 401; session expired → 401; seller banned or soft-deleted → 401.

email.description:
The administrator's registered email address used for authentication.

This email serves as the unique identifier for administrator account lookup during login. It must match an existing, non-deleted administrator record in the system. The email format is validated before database lookup.

For security, a non-existent email and an incorrect password produce the same generic authentication failure response — the system never reveals whether an email address is registered.
email.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from shopping_mall_admins.email. Used as the unique lookup key to find the administrator account. Query filters deleted_at IS NULL to reject soft-deleted accounts. Must be a valid email format. On lookup failure, return 401 without revealing whether the email exists.

password.description:
The administrator's password in plain text for credential verification.

Transmitted to the server where it is compared against the stored hashed password using the same cryptographic algorithm from registration. The password must match the hash stored for the corresponding email address. Both the email and password must be correct for authentication to succeed.

The password is never stored in plain text and never appears in logs or audit records. Authentication failure responses do not indicate whether the email or the password was incorrect.
password.x-autobe-specification: Maps to shopping_mall_admins.password_hash via transformation. Plain text password received in the DTO is compared against the stored hash using the same cryptographic one-way hashing algorithm used during administrator registration. The raw password is never stored or logged. On hash mismatch, return 401 without revealing whether the email or password was incorrect.

href.description:
The full URL of the page where the administrator initiated login.

Captured as part of the session context for audit trail purposes. This information is stored alongside the session record to help track the origin of administrator authentications. Required for all login requests to maintain complete session audit records.
href.x-autobe-specification: Session context property stored in shopping_mall_admin_sessions (not shopping_mall_admins). Captures the full URL of the page where the administrator initiated login. Required for audit trail and security monitoring of administrator access patterns. Must be a valid URI format.

referrer.description:
The URL of the page that referred the administrator to the login page.

Captured as part of the session context for audit trail purposes. This information is stored alongside the session record to help trace navigation paths leading to administrator logins. Required for all login requests to maintain complete session audit records.
referrer.x-autobe-specification: Session context property stored in shopping_mall_admin_sessions (not shopping_mall_admins). Captures the URL of the page that referred the administrator to the login page. Required for audit trail and security monitoring. Must be a valid URI format.

ip.description:
The IP address of the client device initiating the login request.

Captured as part of the session context for audit trail and security monitoring purposes. This field is optional: when provided by the client it is stored directly; when omitted (common in server-side rendering scenarios), the server determines the IP address from the incoming HTTP request as a fallback. Must be in IPv4 format when supplied.
ip.x-autobe-specification: Session context property stored in shopping_mall_admin_sessions (not shopping_mall_admins). Captures the client's IP address for audit trail. Optional because in server-side rendering (SSR) scenarios the client cannot reliably determine its own IP — the server falls back to the incoming request's IP when this field is omitted. Must be IPv4 format when supplied.

IShoppingMallAdmin.ILogin.description:
Administrator login credentials containing the registered email address, password, and session context.

Email and password are validated against stored administrator accounts. The email must match an existing, non-deleted administrator record. The password is transmitted as plain text and compared against the stored hashed password on the server using the same cryptographic algorithm from registration. For security, authentication failure does not distinguish between non-existent accounts and incorrect passwords — both return a generic invalid credentials response.

Session context includes the request origin URL and referrer for audit trail purposes. These fields are required to maintain complete session audit records for security monitoring of administrator access patterns. The IP address is optional: when provided by the client it is stored directly; when omitted (common in server-side rendering scenarios where the client cannot reliably determine its own IP), the server determines the IP from the incoming HTTP request as a fallback.
IShoppingMallAdmin.ILogin.x-autobe-specification: Administrator login request DTO. email maps to shopping_mall_admins.email for account lookup with deleted_at IS NULL filter — soft-deleted accounts cannot authenticate. password is plain text in the DTO body and compared against shopping_mall_admins.password_hash using the same cryptographic one-way hashing algorithm used during registration. For security, authentication failure does not distinguish between non-existent email and incorrect password — both return 401 with a generic message. Session context fields (href, referrer, ip) are captured and stored in shopping_mall_admin_sessions upon successful authentication for audit trail and security monitoring. Excluded: id (auto-generated UUID PK), grade (returned in IAuthorized response, not in login request), created_at and updated_at (auto-managed timestamps), deleted_at (used only as WHERE filter, never exposed in request), adminSessions (created server-side on successful auth), passwordResets and auditLogs (unrelated subsidiary relations).

device_fingerprint.description:
Device fingerprint string for searching guest records.

A device fingerprint uniquely identifies each guest visitor and is generated from client-side device characteristics. This parameter enables administrators to locate specific guests by their fingerprint. Matches can be partial (contains) or exact depending on the implementation.

This field is optional — omit to return all guests regardless of fingerprint.
device_fingerprint.x-autobe-specification: WHERE device_fingerprint CONTAINS value, or exact match depending on implementation. The device_fingerprint column has a @@unique constraint in the database.

created_at_from.description:
Lower bound of the creation date range filter.

Filters guest records to those created on or after this ISO 8601 timestamp. Use together with created_at_to to define a time window for guest account creation (first visit).

This field is optional — omit to leave the lower bound unbounded.
created_at_from.x-autobe-specification: WHERE created_at >= created_at_from. Filters guests created on or after this timestamp. Combined with created_at_to for range queries. The underlying column is shopping_mall_guests.created_at (DateTime @db.Timestamptz).

created_at_to.description:
Upper bound of the creation date range filter.

Filters guest records to those created on or before this ISO 8601 timestamp. Use together with created_at_from to define a time window for guest account creation (first visit).

This field is optional — omit to leave the upper bound unbounded.
created_at_to.x-autobe-specification: WHERE created_at <= created_at_to. Filters guests created on or before this timestamp. Combined with created_at_from for range queries. The underlying column is shopping_mall_guests.created_at (DateTime @db.Timestamptz).

updated_at_from.description:
Lower bound of the last-activity date range filter.

Filters guest records to those whose last activity (updated_at) occurred on or after this ISO 8601 timestamp. Use together with updated_at_to to define a time window for recent guest activity.

This field is optional — omit to leave the lower bound unbounded.
updated_at_from.x-autobe-specification: WHERE updated_at >= updated_at_from. Filters guests whose last activity occurred on or after this timestamp. Combined with updated_at_to for range queries. The underlying column is shopping_mall_guests.updated_at (DateTime @db.Timestamptz).

updated_at_to.description:
Upper bound of the last-activity date range filter.

IShoppingMallGuest.IRequest.description:
Search criteria and pagination parameters for administrators to browse guest visitor records.

Guest visitors are unauthenticated users identified by device fingerprint. This request DTO powers the administrative guest listing endpoint, enabling security auditing, traffic analysis, and monitoring of unauthenticated access patterns.

**Search Filters**

A device fingerprint string can be provided for partial or exact matching against stored guest identities. Date range filters on creation and last-activity timestamps allow narrowing results to specific time windows. The active-only toggle excludes cleaned-up (soft-deleted) guest records.

**Pagination and Sorting**

Results are paginated via page number and configurable page size, with defaults applied when omitted. Default sort order is newest guests first, with direction control available through the sort parameter.

All fields are optional — an empty request body returns all active guests with default pagination.
IShoppingMallGuest.IRequest.x-autobe-specification:
Query the shopping_mall_guests table with flexible search, date-range filtering, active-status toggling, and pagination.

Build a Prisma query with dynamic where clause:
- device_fingerprint: WHERE device_fingerprint CONTAINS (partial match) or exact match depending on implementation preference
- created_at_from / created_at_to: WHERE created_at >= created_at_from AND created_at <= created_at_to
- updated_at_from / updated_at_to: WHERE updated_at >= updated_at_from AND updated_at <= updated_at_to
- active_only: when true, WHERE deleted_at IS NULL; when false or omitted, include all guests regardless of deleted_at

Pagination via skip/take based on page and limit. Default sort: created_at DESC. sort field accepts values like 'created_at_asc', 'created_at_desc', 'updated_at_asc', 'updated_at_desc'.

Authorization: Requires admin authentication. This is an administrative endpoint for security auditing and traffic analysis — no guest or member access.

A guest is an unauthenticated visitor to the platform identified by a unique device fingerprint. Each summary includes the guest identifier, device fingerprint, creation and last-activity timestamps, and soft-deletion status for traffic monitoring and security auditing purposes. Guest records are temporary and may be cleaned up periodically — a non-null deleted_at indicates the record has been purged.

IShoppingMallGuestSession.description:
Full guest session record including audit metadata and the owning guest.

Represents a temporary session token issued to an unauthenticated visitor (guest) when they access the platform. Each session captures the visitor's IP address, the page URL they were on at session creation, and the referring page that led them there, alongside explicit creation and expiration timestamps.

email.description:
Customer's registered email address used as the unique login identifier.

This email address was provided during customer registration and serves as the primary credential for authentication. The system looks up the customer account by this email address, and if found, compares the provided password against the stored cryptographic hash. For security, the system returns identical error responses for non-existent email addresses and incorrect passwords to prevent email enumeration attacks.

Must be a valid email format. The email address is case-insensitive for lookup purposes.

Query: SELECT * FROM shopping_mall_customers WHERE email = :email AND deleted_at IS NULL. If no match, return 401 without revealing whether the email exists (prevent enumeration).

password.description:
Customer's account password provided in plain text for authentication.

This password is transmitted to the server where it is securely compared against the stored cryptographic hash using bcrypt or argon2. The plain text password is never stored in the database, never written to application logs, and never included in any response. If the password does not match the stored hash, authentication fails with a 401 Unauthorized response.

For security, repeated failed authentication attempts are rate-limited to prevent brute-force attacks. The password must match the one set during customer registration.
password.x-autobe-specification: Maps to shopping_mall_customers.password_hash via cryptographic comparison. The plain text password is NEVER stored or logged — it is compared against the stored bcrypt/argon2 hash using a constant-time comparison function. On mismatch, return 401 without revealing whether the email or password was wrong. Rate limiting: max 5 failed attempts per email per minute, max 10 failed attempts per IP per minute.

The href is stored in the session record created upon successful authentication.

Must be a valid URI.

It supports security auditing and traffic source analysis, helping detect unusual login patterns such as direct credential submissions from external sites.

Must be a valid URI.

This optionally provided IP address supports the platform's security infrastructure by enabling per-IP rate limiting and detection of login attempts from geographically anomalous locations. IShoppingMallCustomer.ILogin.description:
Customer login credentials for authenticating into the shopping mall platform.

The email address serves as the unique login identifier used to look up the registered customer account. The password is provided in plain text and securely compared against the stored cryptographic hash on the server side — it is never stored or logged in plain text.

The HTTP referrer (referrer) indicates the previous page the customer navigated from. Supports filtering by client IP address (partial match), session creation date range, active or expired status, and session expiry date range. Results are paginated and returned in reverse chronological order with the most recent logins first.

- created_at_from / created_at_to: WHERE created_at >= from AND created_at <= to.

search.description:
Free-text search applied to both email address and display name.

When provided, results must match at least one of the two fields. Email matching uses partial match (LIKE '%value%'), while display name matching uses full-text search for fuzzy name matching. This enables administrators to find customers by either their login identifier or their public display name in a single query.
search.x-autobe-specification: Combined partial match search across email (LIKE '%value%') and display_name (full-text search via gin_trgm_ops index on shopping_mall_customers). When a value is provided, results must match at least one of the two columns — applied as an OR condition. When absent, no text filter is applied.

ban_status.description:
Filter by account ban status.

Restricts results to customers with a specific ban standing. Use 'banned' to view only accounts that have been banned by an administrator, 'active' to view only accounts in good standing, or omit this parameter (or use 'all') to return accounts regardless of their ban status.
ban_status.x-autobe-specification: Translates to filter on shopping_mall_customers.banned_at column. 'banned' → WHERE banned_at IS NOT NULL. 'active' → WHERE banned_at IS NULL. Absent or 'all' → no filter applied (both banned and active accounts returned).

created_from.description:
Start of registration date range (inclusive).

Filters results to include only customer accounts created at or after this timestamp. Use in combination with created_to to define a precise registration window, or alone to find all accounts registered since a specific date.
created_from.x-autobe-specification: Inclusive lower bound on shopping_mall_customers.created_at column. Applied as WHERE created_at >= value when provided. Can be used independently of created_to to find accounts registered on or after a specific date.

created_to.description:
End of registration date range (inclusive).

Filters results to include only customer accounts created at or before this timestamp. Use in combination with created_from to define a precise registration window, or alone to find all accounts registered up to a specific date.
created_to.x-autobe-specification: Inclusive upper bound on shopping_mall_customers.created_at column. Applied as WHERE created_at <= value when provided. Can be used independently of created_from to find accounts registered on or before a specific date.

include_deleted.description:
Whether to include soft-deleted customer accounts in results.

By default, accounts that have been deleted by their owners are excluded from results. Set this to true when administrators need to audit or review deleted account records. Soft-deleted accounts retain their order history and reviews but have their profile information discarded.
include_deleted.x-autobe-specification: Controls filter on shopping_mall_customers.deleted_at column. When false or absent (default): WHERE deleted_at IS NULL, excluding soft-deleted accounts. When true: no filter on deleted_at, including all accounts regardless of deletion status.

page.description:
Page number for offset-based pagination.

Controls which page of results to return. Page numbering starts at 1, so the first page is page 1. Used together with limit to navigate through large result sets. Defaults to the first page when not specified.
page.x-autobe-specification: 1-indexed page number for offset-based pagination. OFFSET = (page - 1) × limit. Defaults to 1 when not provided. Must be ≥ 1.

limit.description:
Maximum number of records per page.

Defines how many customer account summaries are returned in a single page of results. Limited to 100 records to prevent excessive response sizes and query load. The actual number of records on the final page may be fewer than this limit. Defaults to 20 when not specified.
limit.x-autobe-specification: Maximum number of records per page. Defaults to 20 when not provided. Capped at 100 to prevent excessive result sizes. Must be ≥ 1 and ≤ 100.

IShoppingMallCustomer.IRequest.description:
Search criteria for filtering and browsing customer accounts in the administrative panel.

Provides administrators with flexible query parameters to locate specific customer accounts or audit account standing across the platform. Supports text search across email addresses and display names, filtering by ban status and registration date range, and optional inclusion of soft-deleted accounts.

Pagination parameters control result size and navigation through potentially large customer bases. All parameters are optional — when none are provided, the endpoint returns all non-deleted customers sorted by newest registration first.
IShoppingMallCustomer.IRequest.x-autobe-specification:
Query parameter DTO for filtering and paginating customer accounts in the admin panel. Constructs WHERE clauses on shopping_mall_customers table based on provided filters, with offset-based pagination.

Search behavior:
- `search`: Combined partial match across both email (LIKE '%value%') and display_name (full-text search via gin_trgm_ops index). Applied as OR condition — results match either column.

Filter logic:
- `ban_status`: Maps to banned_at column. 'banned' → banned_at IS NOT NULL. 'active' → banned_at IS NULL. Absent or 'all' → no filter applied.
- `created_from` / `created_to`: Inclusive date range on created_at column. Either bound can be provided independently.
- `include_deleted`: When false (default), filters out soft-deleted accounts (deleted_at IS NOT NULL). When true, includes all accounts regardless of deletion status.

Pagination:
- Offset-based: OFFSET = (page - 1) × limit. Default page=1, limit=20.
- Always sorted by created_at DESC (newest first).
- Limit capped at 100.

Edge cases:
- No filters provided → returns all non-deleted customers (paginated, newest first).
- Empty result set → return empty items array with zero total count.
- password_hash must never appear in any response regardless of filters.

actorType.description:
Filters sessions to a specific actor type.

When specified, only sessions belonging to the selected actor type are included in the results. Supported values:
- customer — registered shoppers
- seller — registered merchants
- admin — platform administrators
- guest — unauthenticated visitors

When omitted, sessions from all four actor types are returned.
actorType.x-autobe-specification: Discriminator filter controlling which session table(s) are included in the UNION ALL query. The value maps directly to a literal actor type tag applied to each row: 'customer' → shopping_mall_customer_sessions, 'seller' → shopping_mall_seller_sessions, 'admin' → shopping_mall_admin_sessions, 'guest' → shopping_mall_guest_sessions. When specified, the UNION ALL is restricted to only the matching table(s); when omitted, all four session tables are queried. This is not a database column — it is a query-level routing parameter.

ip.description:
Filters sessions by IP address.

Accepts a partial or exact IP address string for security auditing and anomaly detection. Matches sessions where the originating IP address contains the provided value.

Use this to trace access patterns across sessions or identify potential credential compromise when sessions from geographically distant IP addresses appear in a short timeframe.
ip.x-autobe-specification: Partial or exact substring match (LIKE '%value%') against the ip column across all queried session tables. The ip column exists with identical String type semantics in all four session tables: shopping_mall_customer_sessions.ip, shopping_mall_seller_sessions.ip, shopping_mall_admin_sessions.ip, and shopping_mall_guest_sessions.ip. In each table, ip captures the client IP address at the moment of session creation for security auditing. This filter is useful for tracing access patterns or detecting credential compromise across geographically distant origins.

actorId.description:
Filters sessions belonging to a specific actor.

Provide the unique identifier (UUID) of a customer, seller, administrator, or guest to retrieve only sessions owned by that actor. When combined with the actorType filter, the lookup is restricted to the matching actor category.

When actorType is omitted, sessions matching this ID are returned regardless of actor type.
actorId.x-autobe-specification: Filter sessions belonging to a specific actor by their unique identifier. Maps to different foreign key columns depending on the actorType context: shopping_mall_customer_id in shopping_mall_customer_sessions (customer), seller_id in shopping_mall_seller_sessions (seller), shopping_mall_admin_id in shopping_mall_admin_sessions (admin), or shopping_mall_guest_id in shopping_mall_guest_sessions (guest). When actorType is also specified, the filter applies only to the matching column in the corresponding table. When actorType is omitted, the filter is applied independently to the appropriate FK column in each of the four session tables. The value must be a valid UUID matching the actor's primary key.

createdFrom.description:
Filters sessions created on or after this timestamp.

Specify an ISO 8601 date-time value as the inclusive lower bound for session creation time. Sessions with a created_at timestamp equal to or later than this value are included in the results.

Use together with createdTo to define a precise time window for reviewing session activity within a specific date range.
createdFrom.x-autobe-specification: Inclusive lower bound for filtering sessions by creation timestamp. Applied as created_at >= :createdFrom across all queried session tables. The created_at column exists with identical DateTime @db.Timestamptz semantics in all four session tables: shopping_mall_customer_sessions.created_at, shopping_mall_seller_sessions.created_at, shopping_mall_admin_sessions.created_at, and shopping_mall_guest_sessions.created_at. In each table, created_at marks the moment of successful authentication and session establishment. May be specified independently of createdTo — when only createdFrom is provided, all sessions created on or after that timestamp are included.

createdTo.description:
Filters sessions created before this timestamp.

Specify an ISO 8601 date-time value as the exclusive upper bound for session creation time. Sessions with a created_at timestamp strictly before this value are included in the results.

Use together with createdFrom to define a precise time window for reviewing session activity within a specific date range.
createdTo.x-autobe-specification: Exclusive upper bound for filtering sessions by creation timestamp. Applied as created_at < :createdTo across all queried session tables. The created_at column exists with identical DateTime @db.Timestamptz semantics in all four session tables: shopping_mall_customer_sessions.created_at, shopping_mall_seller_sessions.created_at, shopping_mall_admin_sessions.created_at, and shopping_mall_guest_sessions.created_at. May be specified independently of createdFrom — when only createdTo is provided, all sessions created before that timestamp are included.

expiredFrom.description:
Filters sessions expiring on or after this timestamp.

Specify an ISO 8601 date-time value as the inclusive lower bound for session expiration time. Sessions with an expired_at timestamp equal to or later than this value are included.

Use together with expiredTo to narrow results to sessions whose expiration falls within a specific time range.
expiredFrom.x-autobe-specification: Inclusive lower bound for filtering sessions by expiration timestamp. Applied as expired_at >= :expiredFrom across all queried session tables. The expired_at column exists with identical DateTime @db.Timestamptz NOT NULL semantics in all four session tables: shopping_mall_customer_sessions.expired_at, shopping_mall_seller_sessions.expired_at, shopping_mall_admin_sessions.expired_at, and shopping_mall_guest_sessions.expired_at. In each table, expired_at defines when the session becomes invalid — sessions past this timestamp are considered expired and the actor must re-authenticate. May be specified independently of expiredTo.

expiredTo.description:
Filters sessions expiring before this timestamp.

Specify an ISO 8601 date-time value as the exclusive upper bound for session expiration time. Sessions with an expired_at timestamp strictly before this value are included.

Use together with expiredFrom to narrow results to sessions whose expiration falls within a specific time range.
expiredTo.x-autobe-specification: Exclusive upper bound for filtering sessions by expiration timestamp. Applied as expired_at < :expiredTo across all queried session tables. The expired_at column exists with identical DateTime @db.Timestamptz NOT NULL semantics in all four session tables: shopping_mall_customer_sessions.expired_at, shopping_mall_seller_sessions.expired_at, shopping_mall_admin_sessions.expired_at, and shopping_mall_guest_sessions.expired_at. May be specified independently of expiredFrom.

isActive.description:
Filters sessions by their active status.

When set to true, only sessions that have not yet expired are returned — these are currently valid authentication sessions. When set to false, only expired sessions are returned for historical audit review.

When omitted, both active and expired sessions are included in the results regardless of their expiration state.
isActive.x-autobe-specification: Computed filter based on whether the session's expiration timestamp is in the future relative to the database server's current time. When true, applies filter expired_at > NOW() across all queried session tables to include only currently valid sessions. When false, applies filter expired_at <= NOW() to include only expired sessions. When omitted, no expiration-based filtering is applied — both active and expired sessions are included. The comparison uses the database server's current timestamp (NOW()) at query execution time, ensuring consistent results regardless of client clock skew.

page.description:
The page number to retrieve.

Pagination is 1-indexed, meaning the first page is page 1. Used together with limit to navigate through large result sets. When omitted, the first page is returned by default.

For example, with a limit of 20, page 2 returns records 21 through 40.
page.x-autobe-specification: Cursor-based pagination: 1-indexed page number for navigating paginated results. Applied as SQL OFFSET = (page - 1) * limit. Defaults to 1 (first page) when omitted. Combined with limit to control the result window. Not a database column — this is a query execution parameter passed to the SQL layer.

limit.description:
The maximum number of session records per page.

Controls how many results are returned in a single response. Must be between 1 and 100 inclusive. When omitted, defaults to 20 records per page.

The actual number of records returned may be less than the limit on the final page or when total matching records are fewer than the requested limit.
limit.x-autobe-specification: Maximum number of session records to return per page. Applied as SQL LIMIT clause. Constrained to minimum 1 and maximum 100. Defaults to 20 when omitted. Combined with page to control the pagination window. Not a database column — this is a query execution parameter.

IShoppingMallGuestSession.IRequest.description:
Search and filter criteria for browsing authentication sessions across the platform.

This request body provides a unified query interface across all four actor types' session tables: customer sessions, seller sessions, administrator sessions, and guest sessions. Sessions are append-only audit records created automatically on successful authentication and terminated on logout, expiration, password change, account deletion, or ban.

All filters are optional — omitting all returns sessions across all actor types. Pagination is controlled via page and limit with a default of 20 sessions per page and a maximum of 100. Results are always sorted by creation time with the newest sessions first.

This endpoint is restricted to administrators for security auditing and access pattern analysis. No actor can modify or delete session records after creation.
IShoppingMallGuestSession.IRequest.x-autobe-specification:
Query across all four session tables — shopping_mall_customer_sessions, shopping_mall_seller_sessions, shopping_mall_admin_sessions, shopping_mall_guest_sessions — using UNION ALL with per-table actor type tagging (discriminator values: "customer", "seller", "admin", "guest").

Apply filters in sequence:
- actorType: when specified, restrict UNION ALL to only the matching session table(s); omit to query all four tables
- ip: partial or exact substring match (LIKE '%value%') against the ip column — this column exists with identical String type semantics in all four session tables, each capturing the client IP address at session creation time for security auditing
- actorId: filter sessions belonging to a specific actor — maps to shopping_mall_customer_id in customer_sessions, seller_id in seller_sessions, shopping_mall_admin_id in admin_sessions, or shopping_mall_guest_id in guest_sessions; when actorType is also specified, the filter applies only to the matching table's FK column; when actorType is omitted, the filter is applied to each table's FK column independently
- createdFrom/createdTo: session creation timestamp range — createdFrom is inclusive lower bound (created_at >= :createdFrom), createdTo is exclusive upper bound (created_at < :createdTo); created_at is a DateTime @db.Timestamptz column present in all four tables; either bound may be specified independently
- expiredFrom/expiredTo: session expiration timestamp range — expiredFrom is inclusive lower bound (expired_at >= :expiredFrom), expiredTo is exclusive upper bound (expired_at < :expiredTo); expired_at is a NOT NULL DateTime @db.Timestamptz column present in all four tables; either bound may be specified independently
- isActive: when true, filter to sessions where expired_at > NOW(); when false, filter to expired_at <= NOW(); omit to include both active and expired sessions

Apply cursor-based pagination (page/limit with SQL OFFSET = (page - 1) * limit, default 20 per page, max 100). Sort by created_at descending (newest sessions first).

Security: restricted to admin actors only. Super admins see all sessions including other admin sessions. Regular admins see all sessions except sessions belonging to other admins (filter out shopping_mall_admin_sessions rows where the admin is not the requesting actor). Sessions are append-only audit records — no write, update, or delete operations are permitted on any session table.

id.description:
Unique identifier of the password reset token record.

The UUID primary key assigned at token creation. Used for retrieval of individual token records and as a unique reference in API paths.
id.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from shopping_mall_customer_password_resets.id. UUID primary key.

expired_at.description:
Timestamp when the password reset token expires.

Tokens carry a fixed validity window from creation (e.g., 1 hour). Once this timestamp has passed, the token is considered expired and cannot be used to authorize a password change. The customer must initiate a new reset request to obtain a fresh token.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when the password reset token was generated.

Records the exact moment the token was created during the forgotten-password flow. Used alongside `expired_at` to calculate the token's remaining validity period and to support chronological listing of a customer's password reset history.
created_at.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from shopping_mall_customer_password_resets.created_at. Timestamptz value.

is_expired.description:
Whether the password reset token has expired.

A convenience boolean flag that evaluates to `true` when the current time has passed the token's `expired_at` timestamp, and `false` otherwise. This eliminates the need for API consumers to perform their own timestamp comparison when checking token validity.
is_expired.x-autobe-specification: Computed as expired_at <= NOW(). No direct database column — purely a convenience flag derived from the expired_at timestamp against the current server time.

IShoppingMallCustomerPasswordReset.ISumm.description:
Summary view of a customer's password reset token record for administrative audit listing.

Each record represents a single password reset request initiated by a customer through the forgotten-password flow. The summary exposes the record's unique identifier, creation timestamp, and expiration timestamp for audit trail purposes.

Security: The cryptographic reset token string is never included in summary responses — only the token's metadata (ID and timestamps) is visible. A computed `is_expired` convenience flag allows consumers to quickly determine token validity without performing their own time comparison.
IShoppingMallCustomerPasswordReset.ISumm.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from shopping_mall_customer_password_resets. Columns id, expired_at, created_at mapped directly. is_expired computed as expired_at <= NOW(). Token column excluded for security — the actual cryptographic reset token must never appear in summary listings. shopping_mall_customer_id excluded — customer context is provided by the parent path parameter (e.g., /admin/customers/{customerId}/password-resets), making the FK column redundant in the summary. The customer relation is also excluded as the summary does not need the full customer object.

id.description:
Unique identifier of the session record.

A UUID v4 value that uniquely identifies this authentication session within the system. Generated when the session is first created after a successful customer login.
id.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from shopping_mall_customer_sessions.id. UUID primary key generated at session creation.

ip.description:
The client IP address from which the customer logged in.

Captured at the moment of session establishment and stored for security auditing purposes. Used to identify unusual login patterns across a customer's session history and to detect potential account compromise through geographic anomalies.
ip.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from shopping_mall_customer_sessions.ip. Client IPv4 address captured at the moment of login for security auditing and anomaly detection.

href.description:
The page URL from which the customer initiated login.

Provides context for the authentication event by capturing the full URL of the page the customer was viewing when they began the login flow. Useful for tracking entry points, analyzing user behavior, and detecting suspicious login origins. This field captures the complete URL and may be quite long.
href.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from shopping_mall_customer_sessions.href. The full page URL where login was initiated. Stored as VarChar(80000) to accommodate long URLs.

referrer.description:
The HTTP Referer header value captured at the time of login.

Records the referring page that led the customer to the login page. Used for forensic analysis of authentication flows and traffic source tracking. May be empty when the browser did not send a Referer header — such as during direct navigation, from a bookmark, or due to privacy settings.
referrer.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from shopping_mall_customer_sessions.referrer. HTTP Referer header value captured at login time. May be an empty string if the browser did not send a Referer header.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when the session was established.

Marks the moment the customer successfully authenticated and this session record was created. Used alongside expired_at to determine the session's active window and to sort sessions in chronological order for history displays.
created_at.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from shopping_mall_customer_sessions.created_at. Timestamptz value set when the session record is created after successful authentication.

expired_at.description:
Timestamp when the session expires or was terminated.

Initially set to the planned expiration time after session creation. Updated to the current timestamp when the session is terminated early — by customer logout, password change, account deletion, or ban. A session is considered active only while the current time is before this timestamp. This field is always present and never null for security reasons.
expired_at.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from shopping_mall_customer_sessions.expired_at. Initially set to planned expiration time. Updated to current timestamp on early termination: logout, password change, account deletion, or ban. NOT NULL — every session must have a definite expiry.

active.description:
Whether the session is currently active.

Computed by comparing the current server time against the expired_at timestamp. Returns true when the session is still valid and its associated tokens can be used for authentication. Returns false when the session has expired naturally or been terminated early by logout, password change, account deletion, or ban.
active.x-autobe-specification: Computed at query time: expired_at > NOW(). Returns true when the session has not yet reached its expiration timestamp, false otherwise. No direct database column — derived expression evaluated in the application layer at query time.

IShoppingMallCustomerSession.ISummary.description:
Summary of a customer's authentication session for list display.

Each session record captures the context of a successful customer login: the client IP address, the page URL where login was initiated, and the HTTP Referer header value. The session remains active until the customer explicitly logs out, the session expires naturally, or the system terminates it due to password change, account deletion, or ban.

The active flag indicates whether the session is currently valid — true when the current time is before expired_at, false otherwise. Sessions are returned in reverse chronological order with the most recent logins first. This summary view is designed for paginated list endpoints where the parent customer is already identified by the path parameter.
IShoppingMallCustomerSession.ISummary.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from shopping_mall_customer_sessions. Six columns mapped directly: id, ip, href, referrer, created_at, expired_at. One computed field: active = expired_at > NOW(). shopping_mall_customer_id is excluded because the parent customer is identified by the {customerId} path parameter in all list endpoints using this summary. The customer belongs-to relation is excluded because the customer context is already established by the URL path — including the parent object would be redundant in a summary view.

from.description:
Earliest creation timestamp for filtering verification tokens.

Limits results to tokens created on or after this ISO 8601 datetime. Use with `to` to define a creation date range window. When omitted, results include all tokens regardless of creation date.
from.x-autobe-specification: Lower bound filter on shopping_mall_customer_email_verifications.created_at (inclusive). Combined with `to` for date range queries. Optional — when omitted, no lower bound is applied.

to.description:
Latest creation timestamp for filtering verification tokens.

Limits results to tokens created on or before this ISO 8601 datetime. Use with `from` to define a creation date range window. When omitted, results include all tokens up to the present.
to.x-autobe-specification: Upper bound filter on shopping_mall_customer_email_verifications.created_at (inclusive). Combined with `from` for date range queries. Optional — when omitted, no upper bound is applied.

expiration.description:
Filter verification tokens by their current validity status.

Restricts results to tokens that are still valid ("active"), already past their expiration ("expired"), or both ("all"). This filter is evaluated against the current server time at query execution.
expiration.x-autobe-specification: Filter on shopping_mall_customer_email_verifications.expired_at status. "active" returns tokens where expired_at > current_timestamp (still valid). "expired" returns tokens where expired_at <= current_timestamp. "all" applies no filter and returns both active and expired tokens. Defaults to "all" when omitted.

page.description:
Page number for paginated results.

Specifies which page of the result set to return. Page numbering starts from 1, and the number of items per page is controlled by the `limit` parameter.
page.x-autobe-specification: 1-based page number for offset-based pagination. Defaults to 1 when omitted. The backend computes offset from (page - 1) * limit.

limit.description:
Maximum number of verification token records per page.

Controls the page size for the paginated response. The actual number of records in a page may be less than this value on the final page or when the total count is smaller than the limit.
limit.x-autobe-specification: Maximum number of records per page. Capped at 100. A platform-default page size (typically 20) is applied when omitted.

sort.description:
Sort direction for verification token results.

Controls the chronological ordering of returned tokens. By default, results are sorted newest first ("desc"). Set to "asc" to view tokens in chronological order from oldest to newest.
sort.x-autobe-specification: Sort direction override for the default created_at ordering. "desc" returns newest tokens first (default). "asc" returns oldest tokens first.

IShoppingMallCustomerEmailVerification.I.description:
Search criteria for browsing a customer's email verification token history.

Provides optional filters to narrow results by when tokens were created (date range) and whether they are currently active or expired. Pagination and sort direction controls allow administrators to efficiently audit verification token activity for a specific customer account.

An empty request body returns all verification records for the customer sorted newest first with default pagination.
IShoppingMallCustomerEmailVerification.I.x-autobe-specification:
Query filter DTO for listing email verification tokens from the shopping_mall_customer_email_verifications table. The customerId path parameter filters results to shopping_mall_customer_id — this DTO provides optional additional filters on creation date range, expiration status, plus pagination and sort controls. All filters are optional and combined with AND logic. An empty request body returns all verification records for the customer sorted newest first with default pagination.

Filters:
- from/to: Date range bounds on shopping_mall_customer_email_verifications.created_at (inclusive).
- expiration: Token validity filter — "active" (expired_at > now), "expired" (expired_at <= now), or "all" (no filter, default).

Pagination: page (1-based), limit (items per page, capped at 100).
Sorting: sort overrides default direction (created_at descending). "asc" for oldest first, "desc" for newest first.

IShoppingMallCustomerSession.description:
A customer authentication session record capturing the complete context of a login event.

Represents a single authenticated session for a customer, created upon successful login. Tracks the client IP address for security auditing, the originating page URL for redirect flows, and the HTTP Referer header value for understanding navigation patterns. When provided together with 'to', restricts results to password resets created on or after this timestamp. The value must be in ISO 8601 date-time format (e.g., '2026-04-01T00:00:00Z'). Providing this parameter without 'to' has no filtering effect.

expiry.description:
Filter password reset records by whether the reset token is currently active or has expired.

Accepted values are 'active' (token has not yet expired and is still usable), 'expired' (token has passed its expiration time and is no longer valid), or 'all' (no expiry filtering — both active and expired tokens are included). When this parameter is omitted altogether, it behaves the same as 'all'.

At query time: 'active' → WHERE expired_at > NOW() (token is still valid), 'expired' → WHERE expired_at <= NOW() (token has passed its expiration time). Omitted or 'all' → no expiry condition applied, returning all records regardless of expiry state. This is a computed comparison — the value is a filter instruction string, not a stored database value.

IShoppingMallSellerPasswordReset.IReques.description:
Search and filter criteria for listing a seller's password reset token history.

This request body provides optional filters to narrow the password reset history of a specific seller. All fields are optional — when omitted, all password reset records for the seller are returned with default pagination.

Date Range Filter

The from and to parameters form an inclusive date range on when password resets were requested. Both bounds must be provided together to activate the range filter; providing only one has no effect.

Expiry Status Filter

The expiry parameter selects tokens by their current validity: 'active' returns only tokens that have not yet expired and are still usable, 'expired' returns only tokens past their expiration time. Omit this parameter or use 'all' to include both.

Pagination

Results are paginated and sorted with the most recent password reset requests appearing first. The page and limit parameters control which slice of results is returned.
IShoppingMallSellerPasswordReset.IReques.x-autobe-specification:
Query filter parameters applied to the shopping_mall_seller_password_resets table, scoped to the seller identified by the {sellerId} path parameter.

Filtering:
- from/to: Optional inclusive date range on created_at. When both supplied, filters WHERE created_at >= from AND created_at <= to. Both must be provided together for the range to take effect; providing only one is ignored.
- expiry: Optional token expiry status filter. 'active' filters WHERE expired_at > NOW(), 'expired' filters WHERE expired_at <= NOW(). Omitted or 'all' returns all records regardless of expiry state.

Pagination:
- page/limit: Offset-based pagination with SQL OFFSET = (page - 1) * limit. Results sorted by created_at DESC (newest first). Default: page=1, limit=20.

Security: The raw token value is never included in request or response bodies. The seller is identified by the URL path parameter, not by any property in this request body.

Maps directly to shopping_mall_products columns: name, description, shopping_mall_category_id, base_price. All fields required.

Authorization:
- The calling user must be an authenticated seller.
- The seller's approval status must be "approved" (verify via shopping_mall_sellers relationship).
- The seller must not be suspended. If suspended, reject with 403 Forbidden.

Validation:
- name: required, non-empty string.
- description: required, non-empty string.
- shopping_mall_category_id: required, must reference an existing category in shopping_mall_categories. If the category does not exist, return 404 Not Found.
- base_price: required, must be a positive number greater than 0 (exclusiveMinimum: 0). If zero or negative, return 400 Bad Request.

Implementation:
- Generate a new UUID for the product id.
- Set shopping_mall_seller_id from the authenticated seller's session.
- Set created_at and updated_at to the current timestamp.
- Insert the row into shopping_mall_products and return the full record.
- Do NOT create a snapshot — snapshots are only created during product edits.
- deleted_at remains null for newly created products.

Excluded from request body: id (auto-generated UUID), shopping_mall_seller_id (JWT session), created_at/updated_at (auto-set), deleted_at (null for new), seller relation (actor identity), category relation (FK exposed as scalar shopping_mall_category_id), all HAS-MANY/HAS-ONE relations (productSnapshots, images, variants, wishlistItems, orderItemProductSnapshots, reviews) — these are composition/aggregation relations managed through separate endpoints.

id.description:
Unique identifier of the guest.

A UUID v4 primary key assigned when the guest first accesses the platform and their device fingerprint is registered. This identifier is embedded in the JWT access token's `sub` claim, enabling downstream services to identify the guest and associate API requests with the correct session and permissions.

Unique device fingerprint identifying the guest visitor.

A string generated from client-side device characteristics — such as browser type, operating system, and screen resolution — that serves as the primary identity mechanism for unauthenticated visitors. The database enforces uniqueness on this field, ensuring no two active guest records share the same fingerprint. This allows the platform to maintain continuity across page visits before the guest registers or logs in as a customer, seller, or administrator.
