sessions.description:
Session records associated with this guest.

Each session represents a temporary authentication window created when the guest registers via device fingerprint or refreshes their tokens. Every session captures audit metadata — IP address, current page URL, and referrer — along with explicit creation and expiration timestamps.

Sessions follow an append-only audit trail pattern: they are never modified or deleted once created. The array includes the current session (just created by the join or refresh operation) along with all historical sessions for the guest. Session validity is determined by comparing the `expired_at` field against the current time — expired sessions remain in the array for audit purposes.

Returns all session records for the guest as an array of IShoppingMallGuestSession. The newly created session from the current join or refresh operation is included alongside all previously created sessions. Sessions are append-only — never updated or deleted.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when the guest account was first created.

Records the exact moment the guest first accessed the platform and their device fingerprint was registered. This timestamp is set once at guest creation and remains immutable through all subsequent sessions and token refreshes. It helps distinguish first-time visitors from returning guests for audit and traffic analysis.
created_at.x-autobe-specification: Sourced from shopping_mall_guests.created_at. ISO 8601 datetime with timezone (Timestamptz). Set once at guest creation and never mutated.

updated_at.description:
Timestamp when the guest account was last updated.

Updated each time the guest establishes a new session — either through the join endpoint (initial registration or re-identification via device fingerprint) or the refresh endpoint (token renewal). This timestamp reflects the most recent activity and helps distinguish active guests from dormant ones for audit and cleanup purposes.
updated_at.x-autobe-specification: Sourced from shopping_mall_guests.updated_at. ISO 8601 datetime with timezone (Timestamptz). Updated each time the guest establishes a new session via join or refresh.

deleted_at.description:

Null for all active guest accounts. Set when the guest record is removed during periodic cleanup of inactive temporary accounts. In the authorization response context, this field is always null because soft-deleted guests are treated as not found — a new guest record with a fresh null `deleted_at` is created instead. Only guests with null `deleted_at` can successfully refresh their tokens.

Non-null indicates the guest was cleaned up during periodic removal of inactive temporary accounts. In the authorization response, this is always null because: (1) soft-deleted guests are treated as not found during join, creating a fresh record; (2) only active guests with null deleted_at can successfully refresh tokens.

token.x-autobe-specification: Authorization token comes from the session table.

IShoppingMallGuest.IAuthorized.description:
JWT token pair issued upon successful guest registration or token refresh.

The authorization response for unauthenticated visitors to the shopping mall platform. Combines three categories of data into a single response: the guest's identity information (unique identifier, device fingerprint, and account lifecycle timestamps), all session records associated with the guest (each capturing audit metadata including IP address, page URL, and referrer), and a JWT-based authorization token bundle for authenticating subsequent API requests.

This response is returned by both the join endpoint — where a guest first registers or is identified via device fingerprint — and the refresh endpoint — where an existing guest exchanges a valid refresh token for new tokens. Guest sessions follow an append-only audit trail pattern: each join or refresh creates a new session while preserving all previous sessions. The access token should be used as a Bearer token in the Authorization header. After the refresh token expires, the guest must re-establish identity through the join endpoint.
IShoppingMallGuest.IAuthorized.x-autobe-specification: Computed JWT authorization response returned by both POST /auth/guest/join and POST /auth/guest/refresh. Guest identity fields (id, device_fingerprint, created_at, updated_at, deleted_at) are sourced from shopping_mall_guests. The sessions array is loaded via the one-to-many relation from shopping_mall_guests to shopping_mall_guest_sessions (JOIN on shopping_mall_guest_id), returning all session records for the guest as IShoppingMallGuestSession instances. The token property is computed entirely at response time: a JWT access token (15-min TTL, signed with server private key, claims: sub=guest.id, session_id=new_session.id), a JWT refresh token (24-hr TTL, same claims), access token expiration datetime (now + 15 minutes), and refreshable_until datetime (now + 24 hours). Tokens are cryptographically signed and never persisted in the database. Served by both POST /auth/guest/join (guest registration/identification) and POST /auth/guest/refresh (token renewal).

Short, human-readable label identifying the category.

When updating, the new name must be unique within its parent scope. For top-level categories, the name must not conflict with any other top-level category. For subcategories, the name must not conflict with any other subcategory under the same parent.

Name uniqueness is enforced within the target parent scope at the service layer (not schema level): two top-level categories cannot share the same name, and two subcategories under the same parent cannot share the same name. If the provided name matches an existing category within the same scope, the service returns HTTP 409.

Contextual explanation of what types of products belong in this category.

Guides sellers in placing products correctly and helps customers understand what they can expect to find within the category. This is a plain text field without formatting or markup.

parentId.description:
Reference to the parent category for the platform's one-level nesting hierarchy.

Set to `null` to make this a top-level category with no parent. Provide a valid top-level category's UUID to place this category as a subcategory under that parent. The platform supports at most one level of nesting — a subcategory cannot itself become a parent to further subcategories.

A category cannot be its own parent, and circular reference chains are rejected at the service layer. The referenced parent category must exist and be active (not soft-deleted).

Direct mapping from shopping_mall_categories.parent_id. Nullable — set to `null` to promote the category to a top-level category (removes the parent relationship). Service-layer validations:
- Parent existence: the referenced category must exist and not be soft-deleted (HTTP 404 otherwise)
- Two-tier hierarchy: the parent must itself be a top-level category — subcategories cannot be parents (HTTP 400 otherwise)
- Circular reference prevention: `parentId` must not equal the category's own ID, and must not create a cycle through the parent chain (HTTP 400 otherwise)

IShoppingMallCategory.IUpdate.description:
Request body for updating an existing product category.

All fields are optional — only the fields provided in the request are modified. Fields omitted from the request retain their current values. Administrators use this endpoint to edit category names and descriptions, reassign parent categories, or promote a subcategory to a top-level category by setting `parentId` to `null`.

The platform enforces a two-tier category hierarchy: a subcategory cannot become a parent to further subcategories, and no category may reference itself as its own parent either directly or through a chain. Category names must remain unique within their parent scope — two top-level categories cannot share the same name, and two subcategories under the same parent cannot share the same name.

Only authenticated administrators may perform this operation. Soft-deleted categories cannot be edited and must be restored before modification.
IShoppingMallCategory.IUpdate.x-autobe-specification:
Maps to shopping_mall_categories table for partial updates. All three fields (name, description, parent_id) are optional — only the properties provided in the request body are applied; omitted fields retain their current values in the database. - `name` must be non-empty when provided (whitespace-only rejected with 400)

search.description:

parentId.description:
Filter categories by parent relationship.

When set to a UUID, returns only subcategories directly under that parent. When explicitly null, returns only top-level categories (those with no parent). When omitted entirely, returns all categories regardless of nesting level. This tri-state design supports three common navigation patterns: browsing the full catalog, viewing a specific parent's children, and viewing only root-level categories.

When explicitly null: WHERE parent_id IS NULL (top-level categories only). When the property is omitted from the request body: no parent_id filtering applied. The parentId filter supports three behaviors: omit to see all categories, set to a UUID to filter by a specific parent, or set to null to see only top-level categories. - **price_asc**: Products are sorted by price from lowest to highest, helping customers find affordable options.
- **price_desc**: Products are sorted by price from highest to lowest, helping customers browse premium products.

IShoppingMallProduct.IRequest.description:
Search, filter, sort, and pagination criteria for browsing products across the platform catalog.

Provides the unified query interface for three customer-facing endpoints: category browsing, full catalog listing, and text-based product search. Every field is optional — when no criteria are specified, the endpoint returns all visible products sorted by newest first with default pagination of 20 items per page.

Product Visibility: The service layer applies mandatory visibility filters before any user-requested criteria. Soft-deleted products, products from suspended sellers, and products from banned sellers are always excluded regardless of the request parameters.

Text Search: The search field supports trigram-based fuzzy matching on product names, allowing customers to find products with partial or approximate search terms. When omitted, all visible products matching other criteria are returned.

Category Filtering: When a category ID is provided, products from that category and all its direct subcategories are automatically included. This enables browsing a parent category and seeing all products in its subtree without separate queries. When omitted, no category restriction is applied.

Price Range: Both minimum and maximum price filters apply to the product's base price. When both are specified, only products with prices between the two bounds are returned. Either filter can be used independently.

In-Stock Filtering: When enabled, only products with at least one variant having positive stock are returned. Stock is computed from the ledger-based inventory system by summing all quantity changes. Products without any variants are always excluded when this filter is active.

Sorting: Results can be ordered by newest first, lowest price first, or highest price first. When variants have price overrides, the effective price (variant override or base price) is used for price-based sorting.

Pagination: Offset-based pagination with a configurable page size between 1 and 100 items. The first page is page 1.

created_at_from.description:
Filter snapshots created on or after this timestamp.

Defines the inclusive start of a creation date window. When combined with created_at_to, snapshots created between the two timestamps (inclusive) are returned. Use this to browse snapshots within a specific time period, such as a particular month or week.

The timestamp must be in ISO 8601 format (date-time).
created_at_from.x-autobe-specification: Date range filter start. Apply WHERE created_at >= :created_at_from. Combine with created_at_to for a closed range. Default sort is created_at DESC. Omit from WHERE clause when not provided.

created_at_to.description:
Filter snapshots created on or before this timestamp.

Defines the inclusive end of a creation date window. When combined with created_at_from, snapshots created between the two timestamps (inclusive) are returned. Use this to cap the time window when browsing historical snapshot data.

The timestamp must be in ISO 8601 format (date-time).
created_at_to.x-autobe-specification: Date range filter end. Apply WHERE created_at <= :created_at_to. Combine with created_at_from for a closed range. Omit from WHERE clause when not provided.

has_parent_snapshot.description:
Filter by whether the variant snapshot belongs to a parent product snapshot.

Variant snapshots are created in two scenarios:
- As part of a product-level edit: the variant snapshot is linked to a parent product snapshot via shopping_mall_product_snapshot_id
- As a standalone variant edit: the variant snapshot has no parent product snapshot

Set to true to see only snapshots from product-level edits. Set to false to see only standalone variant edits. Omit this filter entirely to include both types.
has_parent_snapshot.x-autobe-specification: Filter by parent product snapshot membership. Map to: true → WHERE shopping_mall_product_snapshot_id IS NOT NULL (child of product-level edit), false → WHERE shopping_mall_product_snapshot_id IS NULL (standalone variant edit), omitted → no filter applied.

sku_code.description:
Filter by SKU code with partial matching.

Performs case-insensitive partial matching on the captured SKU code stored in each snapshot. A partial code like "SHO" will match full SKU codes such as "SHO-RED-L" or "SHO-BLK-M".

Use this filter to find snapshots of a specific variant when you know part of its SKU code, or to browse all variants sharing a common SKU prefix.
sku_code.x-autobe-specification: SKU code filter. Apply ILIKE / partial-match on sku_code column. Example: WHERE sku_code ILIKE '%:sku_code%'. Omit from WHERE clause when not provided.

option_values.description:
Filter by option values with partial matching.

Performs case-insensitive partial matching on the captured option values string stored in each snapshot. A search term like "Red" will match snapshots with option values such as "color: Red, size: Large" or "material: Red Cotton".

Use this filter to find snapshots of variants with specific attribute combinations, such as all "Large" variants or all "Red" variants across different product types.
option_values.x-autobe-specification: Option values filter. Apply ILIKE / partial-match on option_values column. Example: WHERE option_values ILIKE '%:option_values%'. Omit from WHERE clause when not provided.

price_min.description:
Minimum variant price filter.

Snapshots with captured prices at or above this value are included. The minimum must be zero or greater.

Important: variant snapshots where price is null — meaning the variant used the parent product's base price at the time — are excluded from price range filters entirely. This is because a null price has no numeric value to compare against. To include these snapshots, omit both price_min and price_max.
price_min.x-autobe-specification: Minimum price filter. Apply WHERE price IS NOT NULL AND price >= :price_min. Null prices (variant using product base price) are excluded from range filters. Omit from WHERE clause when not provided.

price_max.description:
Maximum variant price filter.

Snapshots with captured prices at or below this value are included. The maximum must be zero or greater.

Important: variant snapshots where price is null — meaning the variant used the parent product's base price at the time — are excluded from price range filters entirely. This is because a null price has no numeric value to compare against. To include these snapshots, omit both price_min and price_max.
price_max.x-autobe-specification: Maximum price filter. Apply WHERE price IS NOT NULL AND price <= :price_max. Null prices (variant using product base price) are excluded from range filters. Omit from WHERE clause when not provided.

stock_quantity_min.description:
Minimum stock quantity filter.

Snapshots with captured stock quantities at or above this value are included. The minimum must be zero or greater.

Unlike the price range filters, stock quantity is always a concrete integer value in every snapshot, so null-exclusion logic is not required. Use this filter to find snapshots where a variant had sufficient inventory at the time of the snapshot.
stock_quantity_min.x-autobe-specification: Minimum stock quantity filter. Apply WHERE stock_quantity >= :stock_quantity_min. Stock quantity is never null (stored as integer). Omit from WHERE clause when not provided.

stock_quantity_max.description:
Maximum stock quantity filter.

Snapshots with captured stock quantities at or below this value are included. The maximum must be zero or greater.

Unlike the price range filters, stock quantity is always a concrete integer value in every snapshot, so null-exclusion logic is not required. Use this filter in combination with stock_quantity_min to define a stock level range.
stock_quantity_max.x-autobe-specification: Maximum stock quantity filter. Apply WHERE stock_quantity <= :stock_quantity_max. Stock quantity is never null (stored as integer). Omit from WHERE clause when not provided.

page.description:
Page number for offset-based pagination.

Specifies which page of results to return. Page numbering starts from 1 (the first page is page 1). The number of records per page is controlled by the limit parameter.

Defaults to 1 if not specified. If the requested page exceeds the total number of available pages, an empty result set is returned rather than an error.
page.x-autobe-specification: Page number for offset-based pagination. 1-indexed. Apply OFFSET = (page - 1) * limit. Default: 1. Omit from LIMIT/OFFSET clause when not provided (use defaults).

limit.description:
Number of records per page.

Controls the maximum number of variant snapshot records returned in a single page of results. The value must be between 1 and 100 inclusive.

Defaults to 20 if not specified. Values exceeding 100 are rejected or clamped at the server's discretion to prevent excessive query loads.
limit.x-autobe-specification: Records per page. Apply LIMIT = :limit. Maximum: 100. Default: 20. Validate range [1, 100] server-side — clamp or reject out-of-range values.

IShoppingMallProductVariantSnapshot.IReq.description:
Search and filter criteria for browsing variant snapshot history.

Provides optional filters that narrow variant snapshot query results by creation date, parent snapshot membership, SKU code, option values, price range, and stock quantity range. All filters are optional and can be combined freely — omit a filter to include all matching records for that dimension.

Variant snapshots are immutable audit trail records created automatically when a product variant is edited. This request body is used by both seller-scoped and admin-scoped endpoints to browse snapshot history for a specific variant or for all variants captured within a product-level snapshot.

Results are paginated using offset-based pagination with configurable page size, and sorted by creation time in descending order (newest snapshots first) by default.
IShoppingMallProductVariantSnapshot.IReq.x-autobe-specification:
Computed query filter and pagination parameters for the shopping_mall_product_variant_snapshots table. This DTO carries no direct column mappings — every property represents a WHERE clause filter or pagination control applied when querying variant snapshot records.

Filter logic:
- search: ILIKE/partial match on both sku_code and option_values columns (OR combined)
- created_at_from / created_at_to: WHERE created_at >= :from AND created_at <= :to (BETWEEN range)
- has_parent_snapshot: true → WHERE shopping_mall_product_snapshot_id IS NOT NULL; false → IS NULL; omitted → no filter
- sku_code: ILIKE partial match on sku_code column
- option_values: ILIKE partial match on option_values column
- price_min / price_max: WHERE price >= :min AND price <= :max (null prices excluded from range — use IS NOT NULL guard)
- stock_quantity_min / stock_quantity_max: WHERE stock_quantity >= :min AND stock_quantity <= :max

Pagination: page (1-indexed, default 1), limit (max 100, default 20). Default sort: created_at DESC. All filters are optional and can be freely combined. Actor scoping (seller ownership or admin access) is applied server-side from JWT — not from this request body.

code.description: Globally unique SKU (Stock Keeping Unit) code identifying this variant across the entire platform.

price.description: Optional price override. When set, replaces the parent product's base price. When omitted, the product base price is used.

optionValues.description: Option key-value pairs defining the variant's attributes (e.g., color: "Red", size: "Large"). At least one pair is required. Each key must be unique within the request.

initialStockQuantity.description: Optional initial stock quantity. When provided and greater than zero, an inventory record is created automatically. When omitted, stock starts at zero.

IShoppingMallProductVariant.ICreate.description:
Creation data for a product variant.

A variant represents a specific purchasable combination of option attributes — such as color and size — under a parent product. Each variant is identified by a globally unique SKU code and may optionally override the product's base price.

**Required**: a globally unique SKU code and at least one option key-value pair defining the variant's distinguishing attributes.

**Optional**: a price override (when set, replaces the product base price for this variant; when omitted, the product base price applies) and an initial stock quantity (when omitted, stock starts at zero and an initial inventory record is created automatically).
IShoppingMallProductVariant.ICreate.x-autobe-specification: Maps: code → code, price → price. Composition: optionValues → shopping_mall_product_variant_option_values (nested creation with parent variant id). Each option value requires key and value; key must be unique within the request. Special: initialStockQuantity is not a variant column — when provided and > 0, triggers insertion of an inventory record (shopping_mall_inventory_records) with quantity_change = initialStockQuantity, reason = 'Initial stock'. Excluded: id (auto UUID), shopping_mall_product_id (path parameter productId), created_at/updated_at/deleted_at (auto). Authorization: seller must own the product (verified via shopping_mall_seller_id).

id.description:
Unique identifier of the product.

A UUID v4 string that uniquely identifies this product across the platform. Used for detail page navigation, API references, and linking from wishlists, cart items, and order histories.
id.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from shopping_mall_products.id. UUID primary key, auto-generated on product creation.

name.description:
Display name of the product.

Shown in search results, category listings, and product cards. This is the primary text customers see when browsing products. Must be descriptive enough for customers to identify the product at a glance.

base_price.description:
Default price of the product.

The base price set by the seller at product creation. Individual variants may override this with their own price. When a variant has no price override, this base price is the purchase price. Displayed as the starting or representative price in product listings.
base_price.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from shopping_mall_products.base_price. Double precision float. Serves as the default price when a variant has no price override.

thumbnail_image_url.description:
URL of the product's thumbnail image.

The first product image by display order, used as the main visual representation in search results, category listings, and product cards. Null when the product has no images. The full image gallery is available on the product detail page.
thumbnail_image_url.x-autobe-specification: LEFT JOIN shopping_mall_product_images WHERE shopping_mall_product_id = shopping_mall_products.id AND deleted_at IS NULL, ORDER BY display_order ASC, LIMIT 1. Returns the url of the first image, or null when no images exist for this product.

min_variant_price.description:
Lowest effective price among all product variants.

Calculated from all non-deleted variants' effective prices, where the effective price is the variant's own price override or the product's base price when no override exists. Null when the product has no variants. When all variants share the same effective price or only one variant exists, this equals max_variant_price.
min_variant_price.x-autobe-specification: From non-deleted shopping_mall_product_variants WHERE shopping_mall_product_id = shopping_mall_products.id. For each variant, effective price = variant.price_override ?? shopping_mall_products.base_price. Return MIN of all effective prices. Null when no non-deleted variants exist.

max_variant_price.description:
Highest effective price among all product variants.

Calculated from all non-deleted variants' effective prices, where the effective price is the variant's own price override or the product's base price when no override exists. Null when the product has no variants. When all variants share the same effective price or only one variant exists, this equals min_variant_price.
max_variant_price.x-autobe-specification: From non-deleted shopping_mall_product_variants WHERE shopping_mall_product_id = shopping_mall_products.id. For each variant, effective price = variant.price_override ?? shopping_mall_products.base_price. Return MAX of all effective prices. Null when no non-deleted variants exist.

seller.description:
The seller who owns this product.

Includes the seller's unique identifier, email address, approval status, suspension and ban flags, registration date, and associated shop profile. Provides the shop identity so customers can see which shop offers the product and navigate to the seller's storefront.
seller.x-autobe-specification: BELONGS-TO relation via shopping_mall_products.shopping_mall_seller_id → shopping_mall_sellers.id. LEFT JOIN shopping_mall_sellers and LEFT JOIN shopping_mall_seller_profiles on seller.shopping_mall_seller_id = profile.shopping_mall_seller_id. Returns IShoppingMallSeller.ISummary. Only non-deleted, non-banned sellers are included.

average_rating.description:
Average star rating of the product.

Calculated as the arithmetic mean of all non-deleted customer review ratings for this product. Ranges from 1.0 to 5.0. Null when no reviews exist, indicating the product has not yet been rated — distinct from a zero or low rating.
average_rating.x-autobe-specification: AVG(rating) FROM shopping_mall_review_reviews WHERE shopping_mall_product_id = shopping_mall_products.id AND deleted_at IS NULL. Returns a float between 1.0 and 5.0, or null when no non-deleted reviews exist (indicating 'no rating' rather than zero).

review_count.description:
Total number of reviews for this product.

Counts all non-deleted customer reviews. Used alongside the average rating to indicate review volume — a high average with many reviews carries more weight than one with few reviews.
review_count.x-autobe-specification: COUNT(*) FROM shopping_mall_review_reviews WHERE shopping_mall_product_id = shopping_mall_products.id AND deleted_at IS NULL.

is_purchasable.description:
Whether the product can currently be purchased.

True when at least one non-deleted variant has a stock quantity greater than zero. Products without any purchasable variants are displayed as unavailable in search results and category listings. Products with no variants at all are also unpurchasable.
is_purchasable.x-autobe-specification: EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM shopping_mall_product_variants WHERE shopping_mall_product_id = shopping_mall_products.id AND deleted_at IS NULL AND (SELECT COALESCE(SUM(quantity_change), 0) FROM shopping_mall_inventory_records WHERE shopping_mall_product_variant_id = shopping_mall_product_variants.id) > 0). True when at least one non-deleted variant has positive stock. Products with no variants return false.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when the product was first created.

ISO 8601 date-time string in UTC. Used for sorting products by newest first and displaying product age in listings. Set once at creation and never modified by subsequent edits.
created_at.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from shopping_mall_products.created_at. Timestamptz, set automatically on product creation and never modified.

IShoppingMallProduct.ISummary.description:
Summary representation of a product optimized for list displays in search results and category browsing pages.

Contains essential product identification fields including the unique ID and display name. The thumbnail image provides the main product image — the first image by display order, or null when no images exist. Price information includes the base price as the default price, plus the minimum and maximum variant effective prices showing the price range across all non-deleted variants. When all variants share the same effective price or only one variant exists, both min and max equal that value; when no variants exist, both are null.

The seller provides the shop identity via a seller summary, allowing customers to see which shop offers the product. Customer feedback is represented by the average rating (null when no reviews exist, indicating "no rating") and the review count (total number of non-deleted reviews). The purchasable flag indicates whether the product has at least one variant with positive stock — products without purchasable variants are displayed as unavailable.
IShoppingMallProduct.ISummary.x-autobe-specification:
Summary view of shopping_mall_products optimized for list displays.

Direct column mappings: id, name, base_price, created_at.
Relation: seller — BELONGS-TO via shopping_mall_seller_id → shopping_mall_sellers.id, resolved to IShoppingMallSeller.ISummary (LEFT JOIN shopping_mall_seller_profiles).

Computed properties:
- thumbnail_image_url: LEFT JOIN shopping_mall_product_images, first by display_order ASC WHERE deleted_at IS NULL, returns url or null.
- min_variant_price: MIN(effective_price) from non-deleted shopping_mall_product_variants, where effective_price = variant.price_override ?? base_price. Null when no variants.
- max_variant_price: MAX(effective_price) from non-deleted shopping_mall_product_variants. Null when no variants.
- average_rating: AVG(rating) from non-deleted shopping_mall_review_reviews WHERE product_id = shopping_mall_products.id. Null when no reviews.
- review_count: COUNT(*) from non-deleted shopping_mall_review_reviews WHERE product_id = shopping_mall_products.id.
- is_purchasable: EXISTS non-deleted variant with SUM(shopping_mall_inventory_records.quantity_change) > 0.

Excluded: description (large text), updated_at/deleted_at (system timestamps not needed in summary), shopping_mall_seller_id (FK replaced by seller $ref), shopping_mall_category_id/category (not required in summary listings per design spec), all HAS-MANY relations (images → thumbnail_image_url, variants → price range, reviews → rating/count, productSnapshots/wishlistItems/orderItemProductSnapshots → separate endpoints).

id.description:
The unique identifier of this option value.

This UUID is auto-generated when the option value is first created and cannot be modified. It serves as the primary key for identifying this specific key-value pair within the variant's option set.
id.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from shopping_mall_product_variant_option_values.id. UUID primary key, auto-generated at creation via UUID generation. Immutable after creation — never updated.

key.description:
The option dimension name.

Identifies the attribute category this option value belongs to. Common examples include "color", "size", "material", or "capacity". Each key must be unique within a single variant — a variant cannot have two option values with the same key. Together with the value, this key defines what makes the variant distinct from other variants of the same product.
key.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from shopping_mall_product_variant_option_values.key. The option dimension name (e.g., "color", "size", "material"). Unique within each variant per the @@unique([shopping_mall_product_variant_id, key]) database constraint. Cannot be empty — empty string triggers 400 validation error. When updated via PUT, if the new key conflicts with an existing key on the same variant, a 409 Conflict is returned.

value.description:
The option dimension value.

Specifies the actual attribute for the dimension identified by the key. For example, if the key is "color", the value might be "Red" or "Blue"; if the key is "size", the value might be "Small" or "Large". Together with the key, this value defines what makes the variant distinct from other variants of the same product.
value.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from shopping_mall_product_variant_option_values.value. The specific attribute value for the option dimension (e.g., "Red", "Large", "Cotton"). Cannot be empty — empty string triggers 400 validation error.

created_at.description:
The timestamp when this option value was first created.

Set automatically at the moment the option value record is inserted into the database. This timestamp is never modified after creation, serving as an audit trail of when this specific attribute configuration was introduced to the variant.
created_at.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from shopping_mall_product_variant_option_values.created_at. Timestamptz column, set to the current timestamp at INSERT. Immutable after creation — never updated on subsequent modifications.

updated_at.description:
The timestamp when this option value was last modified.

Updated automatically whenever the option value's key or value is changed, such as when a seller renames an option dimension or updates its attribute value. Set to the same value as created_at when the record is first created.
updated_at.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from shopping_mall_product_variant_option_values.updated_at. Timestamptz column. Set to the current timestamp at INSERT (matching created_at initially). Updated to the current timestamp on every modification to the row, such as when a seller changes the key or value via the PUT endpoint.

IShoppingMallProductVariantOptionValue.description:
A single option key-value pair that defines a distinguishing attribute of a product variant.

Option values describe what makes each variant unique — for example, a clothing variant might have option values for "color" set to "Red" and "size" set to "Large". Each option value consists of a key (the dimension name, such as "color" or "size") and a value (the specific attribute, such as "Red" or "Large").

A variant can have multiple option values, but each key must be unique within the variant — no duplicate dimensions are allowed. Option values are always accessed through their parent variant and product hierarchy. They are subsidiary to variants and do not have standalone access paths.
IShoppingMallProductVariantOptionValue.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from shopping_mall_product_variant_option_values. Read-only response DTO returned by GET (single retrieval), POST (create response), and PUT (update response) endpoints. All fields map directly to columns: id (UUID PK, auto-generated), key (option dimension name, unique per variant via @@unique([shopping_mall_product_variant_id, key])), value (specific attribute value), created_at (Timestamptz, set at INSERT), updated_at (Timestamptz, set at INSERT and updated on every modification). The variant FK (shopping_mall_product_variant_id) is intentionally omitted from the response because consumers already know the variantId from the request path. The variant belongs-to relation is not expanded — option values are subsidiary resources always accessed through their parent variant's URL hierarchy (/products/{productId}/variants/{variantId}/options/...).

id.description:
Unique identifier of the product.

A UUID v4 string assigned automatically when the product is created. This identifier is stable for the lifetime of the product and is used as the primary key in all product-related API operations — retrieving product details, updating product attributes, managing images and variants, and deleting the product.
id.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from shopping_mall_products.id. UUID primary key, auto-generated at product creation. Used as the path parameter in product detail, update, and delete endpoints.

name.description:
Display name of the product.

Shown in search results, category listings, product cards, and the product detail page. Must be descriptive enough for customers to identify the product at a glance. Supports full-text search through the platform's product search endpoint.
name.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from shopping_mall_products.name. Non-empty string. Included in product snapshots when edited. Supports trigram index for full-text search via gin_trgm_ops.

description.description:
Detailed description of the product.

Contains features, specifications, materials, dimensions, and any other information helpful to customers making a purchase decision. Supports rich text formatting for structured presentation on the product detail page. The description is searchable through the platform's product search endpoint, so sellers should include relevant keywords naturally within the text.
description.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from shopping_mall_products.description. Non-empty string. Supports rich text for formatted presentation. Included in product snapshots when edited. Supports trigram index for full-text search via gin_trgm_ops.

base_price.description:
Default price of the product before any variant-specific overrides.

This is the base price that applies to all variants unless a variant specifies its own price override. When viewing a variant, compare the variant's price to this base price to see whether a surcharge or discount applies.

Must be a positive number greater than zero. Sellers can update this value through the product edit endpoint, and every change is captured in the product's snapshot history.
base_price.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from shopping_mall_products.base_price. Float (DoublePrecision), positive number. Serves as the default price when a variant has no price override. Included in product snapshots when edited.

category.description:
The category that classifies this product.

Every product belongs to exactly one category, which organizes products for customer browsing and search filtering. Categories may be top-level or subcategories within the platform's two-tier hierarchy.

The category summary includes the category's name, description, parent category reference, and subcategory count, providing enough context for breadcrumb navigation and category-based filtering. The category is included even if it has been soft-deleted, preserving the product's original classification.
category.x-autobe-specification: BELONGS-TO relation: JOIN shopping_mall_categories ON shopping_mall_category_id → IShoppingMallCategory.ISummary. Include the category even if soft-deleted to preserve historical accuracy — the product's category assignment at creation time remains valid for display even after the category is removed.

seller.description:
The seller's storefront profile.

Identifies the seller who created and owns this product. The profile includes the seller's shop name, shop description, and logo image URI — the public-facing identity that customers see on product pages and in search results.

This is a summary view of the seller profile, providing the essential information for storefront display. Customers can click through to the full seller profile page for more details about the shop.
seller.x-autobe-specification: BELONGS-TO relation: JOIN shopping_mall_sellers ON shopping_mall_seller_id, then LEFT JOIN shopping_mall_seller_profiles ON shopping_mall_sellers.id = shopping_mall_seller_profiles.shopping_mall_seller_id → IShoppingMallSellerProfile.ISummary. The intermediate seller join provides access to approval_status, suspended_at, and banned_at for visibility control. The profile table supplies shop_name, shop_description, and logo_image_uri for display.

images.description:
Gallery images belonging to this product, ordered by display position.

Each product can have multiple images forming a visual gallery that customers browse on the product detail page. The first image — the one with the lowest display order value — serves as the main thumbnail and is used in search results, category listings, and product cards.

Images are ordered by their display_order value in ascending sequence. Sellers can reorder images to control which image appears first and the overall gallery flow. The complete image list is returned so the product detail page can render the full gallery without additional requests.
images.x-autobe-specification: HAS-MANY composition: Query shopping_mall_product_images WHERE shopping_mall_product_id = product.id. Include all non-deleted images ordered by display_order ASC (lowest first = main thumbnail). Each image returns full IShoppingMallProductImage with id, image_url, display_order, and timestamps. Deleting images from this array does not affect previously created product snapshots.

variants.description:
Purchasable variants of this product, each with pricing and stock status.

Every variant represents a specific combination of option values — for example, a clothing product might have variants for 'Red / Small', 'Red / Large', 'Blue / Small', and 'Blue / Large'. Each variant carries a globally unique SKU code for inventory management and order processing.

Pricing for each variant includes both the variant's own price (if an override is set) and the product's base price for comparison. The effective purchase price is the variant's price when set, or the base price when not.

Stock quantity is computed dynamically by summing all inventory ledger entries — a positive value means the variant is in stock and available for purchase. A value of zero or less means the variant is out of stock. Products with no variants at all are displayed as unavailable for purchase.
variants.x-autobe-specification: HAS-MANY composition: Query shopping_mall_product_variants WHERE shopping_mall_product_id = product.id AND deleted_at IS NULL. For each variant: include optionValues from shopping_mall_product_variant_option_values (key-value pairs), compute stock_quantity as SUM of all shopping_mall_inventory_records.quantity_change for the variant, include base_price from the parent product. When a variant has no price override (price IS NULL), the effective purchase price is base_price. Returns IShoppingMallProductVariant.

reviews.description:
Customer reviews for this product, sorted newest first.

Each review includes a star rating from 1 to 5, optional written feedback, and the reviewer's identity. Reviews are written by verified purchasers after their order item reaches delivered status. A customer may write one review per product per order — purchasing the same product across multiple orders allows separate reviews.

Reviews from customers who have deleted their accounts are preserved but the author is shown as 'deleted user' rather than exposing the original display name. Soft-deleted reviews are excluded entirely from this list and from the average rating calculation.

The list is sorted with the most recent reviews first, ensuring customers see the freshest feedback at the top of the page.
reviews.x-autobe-specification: HAS-MANY aggregation: Query shopping_mall_review_reviews WHERE shopping_mall_product_id = product.id AND deleted_at IS NULL, sorted by created_at DESC (newest first). For each review, resolve customer via BELONGS-TO shopping_mall_customers → IShoppingMallCustomer.ISummary. When the authoring customer's deleted_at IS NOT NULL, display author as 'deleted user' rather than the original display_name. Returns IShoppingMallReviewReview.ISummary.

average_rating.description:
Average star rating across all customer reviews for this product.

Calculated as the arithmetic mean of all non-deleted review ratings. A value of null means the product has not yet received any reviews — this is distinct from a low numeric rating and should be displayed to customers as 'no rating' rather than a numerical score.

When reviews exist, the average is a number typically between 1.0 and 5.0. Soft-deleted reviews are excluded from the calculation, so the average reflects only currently visible feedback.

Existing orders that reference this product continue to display correctly using snapshot data.

IShoppingMallProduct.description:
Complete product detail as displayed on the product detail page.

Aggregates everything a customer needs to evaluate a single product: the product's core identity (name, description, category, and base price), the seller's storefront profile, all gallery images in their display order, every purchasable variant with its SKU code, option attributes, pricing, and live stock status, and all customer reviews sorted newest first along with the calculated average rating and total review count.

The product detail page is the destination after a customer clicks on a product from search results or category listings. This DTO provides the full depth of information that the summary view intentionally omits — the complete description text, the full image gallery, all variant options and stock levels, and the entire review history.

Products with no variants are displayed as unavailable for purchase but remain visible so customers can see the product exists. Products from suspended sellers are hidden from customers but remain accessible to the owning seller and platform administrators. Soft-deleted products return 404 for customers and non-owning sellers.

Relation: category — BELONGS-TO JOIN shopping_mall_categories ON shopping_mall_category_id → IShoppingMallCategory.ISummary. Include active and soft-deleted categories to preserve historical accuracy (product may reference a deleted category).

The intermediate seller table provides access control context (approval_status, suspended_at, banned_at); the profile table provides display data (shop_name, shop_description, logo_image_uri).

Compute stock_quantity by SUM of all shopping_mall_inventory_records.quantity_change for the variant. Include base_price from the parent product for comparison with variant's optional price override.

For each review, resolve customer via shopping_mall_customers → IShoppingMallCustomer.ISummary. When the customer is soft-deleted (deleted_at IS NOT NULL), display author as 'deleted user'.

available.description:
Whether the cart item is available for purchase.

Computed at query time by checking three conditions on the referenced product variant: the variant has not been deleted by the seller, the variant has positive stock, and the available stock is sufficient to cover the requested quantity. Returns true only when all three checks pass. Returns false if any check fails.

When the cart item is available for purchase, this field is null. When unavailable, it contains one of three enum values indicating why: "variant_deleted" means the seller has removed this variant from the platform, "out_of_stock" means the variant has no inventory remaining, and "insufficient_stock" means the available stock is less than the requested quantity. The reasons are evaluated in priority order — a deleted variant reports "variant_deleted" even if it would also fail other checks.

When available is false, determined by the first failing check in order: (1) variant_deleted — the referenced variant has a non-null deleted_at timestamp, the seller has removed this variant, (2) out_of_stock — the variant's current stock (SUM of inventory records) is 0, (3) insufficient_stock — the variant has stock but it is less than the cart quantity. The checks are evaluated in this priority order, so a deleted variant with zero stock reports 'variant_deleted', not 'out_of_stock'.

IShoppingMallRefundRequest.IRequest.description:
Search, filter, and pagination parameters for browsing refund request lists.

This request body supports three classes of query parameters: free-text search against the customer-provided refund reason, status-based filtering, and date range filters on both submission and response timestamps. Pagination controls determine result page size and offset.

**Filtering by status**

Refund requests progress through three states in the seller review workflow. Filter by "pending" to see requests awaiting seller action, "approved" to see accepted refunds where processing has completed, or "rejected" to see declined requests.

**Date range filtering**

Two independent date range pairs are available. The created_from/created_to pair filters by when the customer submitted the request. The responded_from/responded_to pair filters by when the seller responded — this pair is only meaningful for non-pending requests since pending requests have no response timestamp.

**Search behavior**

When a search term is provided, results are ordered by relevance against the reason text. Without search, results default to newest-first ordering. All filters combine additively — applying multiple criteria narrows results by all conditions simultaneously.

Query parameters object for paginated refund request search against shopping_mall_refund_requests.

**Search and Filtering**:
- search: Free-text search against the reason column using PostgreSQL trigram similarity (leveraging GIN index). Results ordered by relevance when search is active, by created_at descending (newest first) when browsing without search.
- status: Filter by single status value — "pending" (awaiting seller review), "approved" (seller accepted the refund), or "rejected" (seller declined the refund).
- created_from / created_to: Inclusive date range filter on created_at (request submission timestamp). Both endpoints required together — providing only one has no effect.
- responded_from / responded_to: Inclusive date range filter on responded_at (seller response timestamp). Both endpoints required together. Only meaningful for non-pending requests where responded_at is populated.

**Pagination**:
- page: 1-indexed page number for offset-based pagination. Defaults to 1.
- limit: Maximum records per page, clamped between 1 and 100.

**Server-enforced behaviors (not in request schema)**:
- Soft-deleted records (deleted_at IS NOT NULL) are excluded from results.
- Data ownership isolation enforced server-side based on authenticated actor:
  - Customer: JOIN through shopping_mall_order_items → shopping_mall_orders, filter by shopping_mall_customer_id matching auth actor.
  - Seller: JOIN through shopping_mall_order_items → shopping_mall_product_variants → shopping_mall_products, filter by seller's ID.
  - Admin: No ownership filter — views all refund requests across the platform.
- Default sort: created_at descending (newest first).

Status filtering accepts an array of values from the order item lifecycle: paid (awaiting shipment), shipped (in transit), delivered (confirmed received), cancelled (pre-shipment cancellation approved), and refunded (post-delivery refund approved). Multiple values return items matching any of the specified statuses, enabling views like "all items needing action" across paid and shipped states.

The same request type is used by customers viewing items within their own orders, sellers managing fulfillment across all their products, and administrators performing platform-wide oversight. Each actor's backend handler applies its own authorization scoping and default sort ordering.

A cursor value for cursor-based pagination, enabling stable and efficient traversal of large result sets.

When provided, the server switches from offset-based to cursor-based pagination: it returns records positioned after this cursor based on the current sort field and direction. For descending sort (the default: newest first), the query filters WHERE sortField < cursor. For ascending sort, WHERE sortField > cursor.

Cursor-based pagination is recommended for large review datasets as it maintains consistent performance regardless of page depth, unlike offset-based pagination which degrades with higher page numbers.
cursor.x-autobe-specification: Cursor-based pagination token: the value of the current sort field from the last item of the previous page. Applied as WHERE {sortField} < cursor (for DESC sort) or WHERE {sortField} > cursor (for ASC sort), combined with LIMIT {limit}. When this field is provided, offset-based pagination (page) is ignored. Not mapped to any database column — purely a query-layer parameter.

sortField.description:
The database column to sort review results by.

Supported sort fields map directly to columns on the reviews table:
- **created_at** (default): Order reviews by their original submission date. This is the default and matches the product detail page display where newest reviews appear first.
- **rating**: Order reviews by star rating. Combined with ascending direction, this groups critical reviews (low ratings) first; with descending, it surfaces the most positive reviews.
- **updated_at**: Order reviews by their most recent modification timestamp — including edits, rating changes, and soft-deletions. Useful for finding recently modified reviews.
sortField.x-autobe-specification:
Column to sort results by. Maps to SQL ORDER BY clause on the shopping_mall_review_reviews table:
- 'created_at' (default) → shopping_mall_review_reviews.created_at (timestamptz, review submission timestamp)
- 'rating' → shopping_mall_review_reviews.rating (integer, star rating 1-5)
- 'updated_at' → shopping_mall_review_reviews.updated_at (timestamptz, last modification timestamp)

The sort direction is controlled by sortDirection. Defaults to 'created_at' when not specified.

sortDirection.description:
The direction to sort results.

- **desc** (default): Descending order — newest reviews first, highest ratings first, most recently updated first. This matches the product detail page display where customers expect to see the most recent feedback at the top.
- **asc**: Ascending order — oldest reviews first, lowest ratings first, least recently updated first. Useful for chronological browsing or auditing review histories.
sortDirection.x-autobe-specification: Sort direction for the ORDER BY clause. Applied as ORDER BY {sortField} ASC or DESC. Defaults to 'desc' (newest first). Not mapped to any database column — purely a query-layer parameter that controls the direction of the SQL ORDER BY clause.

contentSearch.description:
A free-text search term to find reviews containing specific words or phrases in their written feedback.

Performs a case-insensitive partial match against the review's optional written content. For example, searching for "quality" returns all reviews whose content contains the word "quality" anywhere in the text, regardless of capitalization.

Reviews that consist solely of a star rating with no written content are never matched by this filter. The search supports natural language phrases — multi-word terms match reviews containing those words in sequence.
contentSearch.x-autobe-specification: Case-insensitive partial text match on the shopping_mall_review_reviews.content column. Applied as WHERE content ILIKE '%' || contentSearch || '%'. The content column is nullable — reviews with NULL content are never matched by this filter regardless of the search term. When available, leverages the PostgreSQL trigram (gin_trgm_ops) index on the content column for efficient partial matching. All special SQL characters in the search term should be properly escaped to prevent injection.

customerId.description:
Filter reviews to only those written by a specific customer.

Accepts a customer's unique identifier as a UUID. When the authorized actor is a customer, this field is automatically resolved from their authentication token to scope results to their own reviews — customers cannot browse reviews written by other customers through this filter.

Administrators can specify any customer ID to audit all reviews authored by a particular user. Reviews written by customers who later deleted their accounts are still findable — the review content and rating are preserved while the author is displayed as 'deleted user' in the response.
customerId.x-autobe-specification: Equality filter on the shopping_mall_review_reviews.shopping_mall_customer_id column (UUID, foreign key to shopping_mall_customers). Applied as WHERE shopping_mall_customer_id = customerId. When the authorized actor is a customer, this value is resolved from the JWT token and any user-supplied value is overridden at the service layer to enforce data isolation — customers can only view their own reviews.

productId.description:
Filter reviews to only those written for a specific product.

Accepts a product's unique identifier as a UUID. In the product-specific review listing endpoint, the product ID is provided as a path parameter and this field is typically omitted from the request body.

In the global review search endpoint, this filter enables browsing all reviews for a particular product across all orders and customers. Reviews for soft-deleted products remain accessible — the review data is preserved for historical accuracy even after a product is removed from the marketplace.
productId.x-autobe-specification: Equality filter on the shopping_mall_review_reviews.shopping_mall_product_id column (UUID, foreign key to shopping_mall_products). Applied as WHERE shopping_mall_product_id = productId. In the product-specific endpoint (PATCH /shoppingMall/products/{productId}/reviews), the productId path parameter takes precedence — this field may be omitted or is overridden by the path parameter.

orderId.description:
Filter reviews to only those associated with a specific order.

Accepts an order's unique identifier as a UUID. This filter is useful for administrative audit scenarios where all reviews originating from a particular order need to be examined — for example, investigating a pattern of suspicious reviews tied to a single purchase.

The uniqueness constraint on reviews allows one review per product per order, so a single order may contain multiple reviews across different products. This filter returns all of them.
orderId.x-autobe-specification: Equality filter on the shopping_mall_review_reviews.shopping_mall_order_id column (UUID, foreign key to shopping_mall_orders). Applied as WHERE shopping_mall_order_id = orderId. Used primarily in administrative audit workflows to trace all reviews originating from a specific order.

orderItemId.description:
Filter reviews to only those linked to a specific order item.

Accepts an order item's unique identifier as a UUID. Each review is tied to the exact order item whose delivered status enabled the review — the customer must have received that specific variant before they can write a review for the product.

This provides the most granular level of review traceability, directly connecting a review to the purchase line item that qualified the customer to provide feedback.
orderItemId.x-autobe-specification: Equality filter on the shopping_mall_review_reviews.shopping_mall_order_item_id column (UUID, foreign key to shopping_mall_order_items). Applied as WHERE shopping_mall_order_item_id = orderItemId. This is the most granular review filter — each review is linked to the specific order item whose delivered status qualified the customer to write it.

rating.description:
Filter reviews to only those with an exact star rating.

Accepts an integer from 1 to 5 inclusive, representing the star rating. This filter is primarily used on product detail pages to let customers browse only 5-star reviews or only critical 1-star reviews for a product.

When both the exact rating filter and the rating range filters (ratingMin/ratingMax) are provided in the same request, the exact rating filter takes precedence. In typical usage, either rating or ratingMin/ratingMax is provided, but not both.
rating.x-autobe-specification: Exact equality filter on the shopping_mall_review_reviews.rating column (integer, non-null, application-constrained to 1-5). Applied as WHERE rating = [value]. This filter is primarily used by the product-specific endpoint (PATCH /shoppingMall/products/{productId}/reviews) to let customers browse reviews filtered to a specific star rating. When both rating and ratingMin/ratingMax are provided in the same request, the exact rating filter takes precedence as the more specific constraint.

ratingMin.description:
The minimum star rating to include in results, inclusive.

Accepts an integer from 1 to 5. Combined with ratingMax, this creates a rating range filter. For example, setting ratingMin to 4 returns all reviews rated 4 stars and above — useful for browsing only positive feedback.

When only ratingMin is provided without ratingMax, the filter acts as a floor: all reviews with a rating at or above this value are returned. Setting both ratingMin and ratingMax to the same value is equivalent to using the exact rating filter.
ratingMin.x-autobe-specification: Lower bound (inclusive) for a range filter on the shopping_mall_review_reviews.rating column (integer, non-null, application-constrained to 1-5). Applied as WHERE rating >= ratingMin. Combine with ratingMax to create a bounded range. When only ratingMin is provided without ratingMax, all reviews with rating >= ratingMin are returned.

ratingMax.description:
The maximum star rating to include in results, inclusive.

Accepts an integer from 1 to 5. Combined with ratingMin, this creates a rating range filter. For example, setting ratingMax to 2 returns only critical reviews rated 2 stars and below — useful for identifying products with quality concerns.

When only ratingMax is provided without ratingMin, the filter acts as a ceiling: all reviews with a rating at or below this value are returned. Setting both ratingMin and ratingMax to the same value is equivalent to using the exact rating filter.
ratingMax.x-autobe-specification: Upper bound (inclusive) for a range filter on the shopping_mall_review_reviews.rating column (integer, non-null, application-constrained to 1-5). Applied as WHERE rating <= ratingMax. Combine with ratingMin to create a bounded range. When only ratingMax is provided without ratingMin, all reviews with rating <= ratingMax are returned (including 1-star reviews).

createdFrom.description:
The earliest review submission date to include, inclusive.

Accepts an ISO 8601 datetime string (e.g., "2025-01-01T00:00:00Z"). Combined with createdTo, this creates a time window filter for when reviews were originally submitted.

Example: setting createdFrom to the start of a month and createdTo to its end returns all reviews first written during that calendar month, regardless of any later edits.
createdFrom.x-autobe-specification: Lower bound (inclusive) for a range filter on the shopping_mall_review_reviews.created_at column (timestamptz, non-null, set at review submission time). Applied as WHERE created_at >= createdFrom. Combine with createdTo to define a time window. The created_at column records when the review was originally submitted and is never modified — it differs from updated_at which changes on edits and deletions.

createdTo.description:
The latest review submission date to include, inclusive.

Accepts an ISO 8601 datetime string (e.g., "2025-12-31T23:59:59Z"). Combined with createdFrom, this creates a time window filter for when reviews were originally submitted.

This filter uses the original creation timestamp, not the last-modified timestamp. Reviews edited after this window but originally created within it are still included.
createdTo.x-autobe-specification: Upper bound (inclusive) for a range filter on the shopping_mall_review_reviews.created_at column (timestamptz, non-null, set at review submission time). Applied as WHERE created_at <= createdTo. Combine with createdFrom to define a time window. The created_at column is never modified after initial insert.

updatedFrom.description:
The earliest review modification date to include, inclusive.

Accepts an ISO 8601 datetime string. Combined with updatedTo, this creates a time window filter for when reviews were last modified — including rating changes, content edits, and soft-deletions.

This filter is useful for finding recently edited reviews that may warrant re-examination or for audit workflows tracking review modification patterns over time.
updatedFrom.x-autobe-specification: Lower bound (inclusive) for a range filter on the shopping_mall_review_reviews.updated_at column (timestamptz, non-null, updated on every modification). Applied as WHERE updated_at >= updatedFrom. The updated_at column tracks the most recent change to the review including rating edits, content modifications, and soft-deletion (which sets deleted_at but also updates updated_at).

updatedTo.description:
The latest review modification date to include, inclusive.

Accepts an ISO 8601 datetime string. Combined with updatedFrom, this bounds the modification date window for filtering reviews that were changed within a specific time period.

Note that this filter captures all types of modifications — edits, rating changes, and soft-deletions all update the same timestamp. To distinguish between these, check the response data rather than relying on the filter alone.
updatedTo.x-autobe-specification: Upper bound (inclusive) for a range filter on the shopping_mall_review_reviews.updated_at column (timestamptz, non-null, updated on every modification). Applied as WHERE updated_at <= updatedTo. Combine with updatedFrom to define a time window for review modifications.

includeDeleted.description:
Whether to include soft-deleted reviews in the results.

By default (false or omitted), soft-deleted reviews are excluded from all listings — they are hidden from product detail pages and excluded from average rating calculations, consistent with the customer-facing behavior of the platform.

Setting this to true overrides that behavior and includes reviews where deleted_at is not null. This override is restricted to administrator accounts for moderation and audit workflows — for example, reviewing a pattern of deleted reviews that may indicate abuse.

Non-administrator requests with includeDeleted set to true are rejected with a 403 Forbidden error.
includeDeleted.x-autobe-specification: Controls the WHERE deleted_at IS NULL default filter on the shopping_mall_review_reviews.deleted_at column (timestamptz, nullable — null means active, non-null means soft-deleted). When false or omitted: WHERE deleted_at IS NULL (default — soft-deleted reviews are excluded). When true: the deleted_at filter is omitted entirely, returning both active and soft-deleted reviews. This override is restricted to administrator accounts — non-admin requests with includeDeleted: true must be rejected with HTTP 403 Forbidden or silently overridden to false at the service layer.

IShoppingMallReviewReview.IRequest.description:
Search criteria for filtering, sorting, and paginating product reviews across the shopping mall platform.

This DTO powers two distinct endpoints: the product-specific review listing on the product detail page and the global cross-product review search. All filter fields are optional — when none are provided, the default behavior returns non-deleted reviews sorted newest first.

**Filtering capabilities**: Narrow results by individual product, customer, order, or order item using UUID equality filters. Filter by exact star rating or a rating range to surface reviews of a specific quality tier. Search review content for keywords or phrases using case-insensitive partial matching. Date range filters support browsing reviews created or modified within a specific time window.

**Soft-delete handling**: Soft-deleted reviews are excluded from results by default, consistent with their removal from product detail pages and exclusion from average rating calculations. Administrators may set includeDeleted to true to view deleted reviews for moderation and audit purposes.

**Sorting and pagination**: Results are sorted newest first by default, matching the display order on product detail pages. Alternative sorting by star rating or last-modified date is supported. Both cursor-based and offset-based pagination are available, with a configurable page size capped at 100 records.
IShoppingMallReviewReview.IRequest.x-autobe-specification:
Query and filter DTO for the shopping_mall_review_reviews table. This is a pure query-layer DTO — all fields are optional filter, sort, and pagination parameters applied at the SQL query level. No direct table mapping at the object level; each property maps to a specific column or query construct on the reviews table.

**Source table**: shopping_mall_review_reviews

**Default soft-delete filter**: Always apply WHERE deleted_at IS NULL on the shopping_mall_review_reviews.deleted_at column unless includeDeleted is explicitly set to true by an authorized administrator. This ensures soft-deleted reviews are hidden from product detail pages and excluded from average rating calculations.

**ID equality filters**: When provided, apply WHERE equality clauses:
- customerId → shopping_mall_review_reviews.shopping_mall_customer_id
- productId → shopping_mall_review_reviews.shopping_mall_product_id
- orderId → shopping_mall_review_reviews.shopping_mall_order_id
- orderItemId → shopping_mall_review_reviews.shopping_mall_order_item_id

**Rating filters**:
- When `rating` is provided (used by product-specific endpoint PATCH /shoppingMall/products/{productId}/reviews): WHERE shopping_mall_review_reviews.rating = [value]
- When `ratingMin` and/or `ratingMax` are provided (used by global search endpoint PATCH /shoppingMall/customer/reviews): WHERE shopping_mall_review_reviews.rating >= ratingMin AND shopping_mall_review_reviews.rating <= ratingMax
- Both bounds are inclusive. The rating column is a non-null integer constrained to 1-5 at the application layer.

**Date range filters**:
- createdFrom/createdTo → WHERE shopping_mall_review_reviews.created_at >= createdFrom AND shopping_mall_review_reviews.created_at <= createdTo
- updatedFrom/updatedTo → WHERE shopping_mall_review_reviews.updated_at >= updatedFrom AND shopping_mall_review_reviews.updated_at <= updatedTo
- Both bounds are inclusive. Uses timestamptz columns.

**Content search**: contentSearch → WHERE shopping_mall_review_reviews.content ILIKE '%' || contentSearch || '%' (case-insensitive partial match). Reviews with NULL content are never matched. Leverages the PostgreSQL trigram index on the content column when available.

**Sorting**: ORDER BY {sortField} {sortDirection}:
- sortField maps to shopping_mall_review_reviews columns: 'created_at' → created_at, 'rating' → rating, 'updated_at' → updated_at
- sortDirection: 'asc' → ASC, 'desc' → DESC
- Default: created_at DESC (newest first), matching the product detail page display order and leveraging the index on (shopping_mall_product_id, created_at).

**Pagination — offset-based**: OFFSET (page - 1) * limit, LIMIT {limit}. When page is provided and cursor is not.
**Pagination — cursor-based**: WHERE {sortField} < cursor (for DESC) or > cursor (for ASC), LIMIT {limit}. When cursor is provided, page is ignored.
**Limit**: default 20, hard maximum 100.
**Total count**: Always compute COUNT(*) of the filtered result set (before LIMIT/OFFSET) to populate IPage.IPagination.records.

**All filters are combined conjunctively (AND).** All filter fields are optional — when none are provided, the query returns all non-deleted reviews sorted newest first.

**Access control** (enforced at the middleware/service layer, not in this DTO):
- Guests: denied entirely.
- Customers: may query their own reviews; customerId is resolved from JWT and overrides any user-supplied value.
- Sellers: may filter reviews for their own products; scoped at the service layer.
- Administrators: unrestricted access including the includeDeleted override.
- Non-admin requests with includeDeleted: true are rejected with 403 or silently overridden to false.

**Deleted user handling**: When a review's author has deleted their customer account, the review content and rating are preserved. The author attribution as 'deleted user' is handled in the ISummary response layer, not in the filtering logic. Deleted customers' reviews still appear in query results (they are not filtered out).

IShoppingMallOrderItem.description:
A single line item within a customer order, representing the purchase of a specific product variant with the quantity and unit price frozen at the moment of order creation.

Each order item has an independent lifecycle status — paid, shipped, delivered, cancelled, or refunded — that progresses separately from other items in the same order. The price is captured once at purchase and never changes, ensuring historical accuracy regardless of later product or variant price adjustments.

The response includes purchase-time snapshots of the product, variant, and seller profile, preserving the exact context at the moment of purchase. This historical integrity is maintained even if the underlying products, variants, or seller profiles have since been modified, suspended, or deleted. If the item has been assigned to a shipment by the seller, the associated carrier name and tracking number are included. Any active cancellation or refund requests linked to this item are also returned.

Direct columns from shopping_mall_order_items: id, quantity, price, status, created_at, updated_at.

BELONGS-TO relations (replacing FK columns with ISummary objects):
- order → IShoppingMallOrder.ISummary via shopping_mall_order_id JOIN on shopping_mall_orders (code, status, created_at)
- variant → IShoppingMallProductVariant.ISummary via shopping_mall_product_variant_id JOIN on shopping_mall_product_variants (id, code) with optionValues from shopping_mall_product_variant_option_values
- shipment → IShoppingMallShipment.ISummary | null via nullable shopping_mall_shipment_id JOIN on shopping_mall_shipments (carrier_name, tracking_number, delivered_at, created_at)

1:1 snapshot relations (all nullable per DB optional relations — handle missing gracefully):
- productSnapshot → IShoppingMallOrderItemProductSnapshot | null via shopping_mall_order_item_product_snapshots (join on shopping_mall_order_item_id unique)
- variantSnapshot → IShoppingMallOrderItemVariantSnapshot | null via shopping_mall_order_item_variant_snapshots (join on shopping_mall_order_item_id unique)
- sellerSnapshot → IShoppingMallOrderItemSellerSnapshot | null via shopping_mall_order_item_seller_snapshots (join on shopping_mall_order_item_id unique)
